```
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.InputAccess

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Bounded runs and counting loops of abstract register machines

The guard `Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe A x B` of bounded runs of an abstract register machine
(`Complexity.LogProg.ARM`): a configuration meets it when it satisfies the syntactic
preconditions `Complexity.LogProg.PreS` and all its registers are at most `B`. It is
definitionally the guard of the shared fragments of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.InputAccess` (`registerCopy_loop`, …), so their
runs compose with runs through `GuardLe`. It is used by the codec checkers
(`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Codec.Engine`) and the Savitch machine
(`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM`).

The file also proves run lemmas for the counting loops out of which register-machine
arithmetic is built: moving a register into one or two others (`move_run`, `move2_run`),
moving it doubled (`dmove_run`), subtracting (`sub_run`), halving a register as often as a
counter says (`halve_run`), copying through a scratch register (`copy_run`) and shifting left
by a counter (`shl_run`). Each lemma is stated for an arbitrary abstract register machine
whose instructions at the loop's labels have the loop's shape, as a run through `GuardLe`.

Infrastructure for the register-machine description of space-bounded algorithms of
[AB09, §4.1]; not itself a result of the book.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe` — the guard: syntactic preconditions and registers at most
  `B`.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe.of_preS` — introducing the guard.
* `Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.embed_guardLe` — a bounded halting run of a block, inside a
  larger machine.
* `Complexity.LogProg.reach_of_eq` — rewriting the end configuration of a run.
* `Complexity.LogProg.move_run`, `move2_run`, `dmove_run`, `sub_run`, `halve_run` — the
  single loops.
* `Complexity.LogProg.copy_run`, `shl_run` — the composite loops.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

open Turing

variable {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type}

/-- **The bounded-run guard**: the syntactic preconditions, and every register at most `B`. -/
abbrev GuardLe (A : ARM m d Λ) (x : List Bool) (B : ℕ) : AConf m Λ → Prop :=
  fun a => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B

variable {A : ARM m d Λ} {oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {B : ℕ}

/-- A configuration meeting the syntactic preconditions with registers at most `B` meets the
guard. -/
lemma GuardLe.of_preS {a : AConf m Λ} (h : PreS A x a) (hv : ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ B) :
    GuardLe A x B a := ⟨h, hv⟩

/-- **A bounded halting run of a block, inside a larger machine**: if `A`, its deciders read
through `σ`, answers `b` from `l` with registers at most `B`, then a larger machine holding
`A`'s table as a block (`Complexity.LogProg.Ins.embed`) runs from the image of `l` to the exit
`k b` with registers at most `B' ≥ B`, provided its own registers (`e`, off `ρ`'s range) are at
most `B'`. It ends with the block's registers at most `B` and its own registers unchanged.

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.LogProg.AHalt.embed`; the guard carries over because the
syntactic preconditions do (`Complexity.LogProg.preS_embed`) and every register of the larger
machine is either an image of one of `A`'s or one of its own. -/
theorem AHalt.embed_guardLe {m' d' : ℕ} {Λ' : Type} {D : ARM m' d' Λ'} {ρ : Fin m → Fin m'}
    {σ : Fin d → Fin d'} {ι : Λ → Λ'} {k : Bool → Λ'} {r₀ : Fin m'}
    (hρ : Function.Injective ρ) (hD : ∀ l, D (ι l) = (A l).embed ρ σ ι k r₀)
    (hA : ∀ l r l', A l ≠ .valP r l' ∧ A l ≠ .valQ r l') {oracle' : Fin d' → List Bool → Bool}
    {B' : ℕ} (hBB : B ≤ B') {e : Fin m' → ℕ} (he : ∀ r', e r' ≤ B') {l : Λ} {v : Fin m → ℕ}
    {b : Bool} (h : AHalt A (oracle' ∘ σ) x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none) b)
    {v' : Fin m' → ℕ} (hv : RegExt ρ e v v') :
    ∃ v₂', (∀ r', (∀ r, ρ r ≠ r') → v₂' r' = e r') ∧ (∀ r, v₂' (ρ r) ≤ B) ∧
      AReach D oracle' x (GuardLe D x B') (some (ι l), v', none) (some (k b), v₂', none) := by
  have hG : ∀ l v v', GuardLe A x B (some l, v, none) → RegExt ρ e v v' →
      GuardLe D x B' (some (ι l), v', none) := by
    intro l v v' hg hv
    refine ⟨preS_embed hρ hD hg.1, fun r' => ?_⟩
    show v' r' ≤ B'
    by_cases hr : ∃ r, ρ r = r'
    · obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hr
      rw [hv.reg]
      exact (hg.2 r).trans hBB
    · push_neg at hr
      rw [hv.ext r' hr]
      exact he r'
  obtain ⟨v₂, v₂', ⟨l₂, hg₂⟩, hv₂, hr⟩ := AHalt.embed hρ hD hA hG h hv
  exact ⟨v₂', hv₂.ext, fun r => (hv₂.reg r).symm ▸ hg₂.2 r, hr⟩

/-- A run whose end configuration is rewritten along an equation. -/
lemma reach_of_eq {G : AConf m Λ → Prop} {a b b' : AConf m Λ} (h : AReach A oracle x G a b)
    (e : b = b') : AReach A oracle x G a b' := e ▸ h

/-! ## Counting loops -/

/-- **Moving a register into another**: the loop `l: jz r lx l₁; l₁: dec r l₂; l₂: inc t l`
adds `r` to `t` and clears `r`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the value of `r`: each round moves one unit. -/
theorem move_run {l lx l1 l2 : Λ} {r t : Fin m} (hrt : r ≠ t)
    (h0 : A l = .jz r lx l1) (h1 : A l1 = .dec r l2) (h2 : A l2 = .inc t l) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ), v r = k → (∀ s, v s ≤ B) → v t + v r ≤ B →
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update (Function.update v r 0) t (v t + v r), none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v hk hv _
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    have e : Function.update (Function.update v r 0) t (v t + v r) = v := by
      funext s
      by_cases hs : s = t
      · subst hs; simp [hk]
      · by_cases hs' : s = r
        · subst hs'; simp [hs, hk]
        · simp [hs, hs']
    rw [e]
    simp only [astep, h0, hk, ↓reduceIte]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v hk hv hb
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h0, hk, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h1], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h1, hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h2], fun s => ?_⟩ ?_
    · by_cases hs : s = r
      · subst hs; simp; omega
      · simp [hs]; exact hv s
    simp only [astep, h2, Function.update_of_ne (Ne.symm hrt)]
    have hb2 : ∀ s, Function.update (Function.update v r k) t (v t + 1) s ≤ B := by
      intro s
      by_cases hs : s = t
      · subst hs; simp; omega
      · by_cases hs' : s = r
        · subst hs'; simp [hs]; omega
        · simp [hs, hs']; exact hv s
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ (by simp [hrt]) hb2 (by simp [hrt]; omega)) ?_
    · congr 2
      funext s
      by_cases hs : s = t
      · subst hs; simp [hrt]; omega
      · by_cases hs' : s = r
        · subst hs'; simp [hs]
        · simp [hs, hs']

/-- Close a goal about updated register files by cases on the register. -/
local macro "upd_tac" : tactic =>
  `(tactic| (funext s; simp only [Function.update_apply]; split_ifs <;> subst_vars <;>
    (try simp_all) <;> omega))

/-- **Moving a register into two others**: the loop
`l: jz r lx l₁; l₁: dec r l₂; l₂: inc t l₃; l₃: inc t' l` adds `r` to `t` and to `t'` and
clears `r`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the value of `r`: each round moves one unit into both. -/
theorem move2_run {l lx l1 l2 l3 : Λ} {r t t' : Fin m} (hrt : r ≠ t) (hrt' : r ≠ t')
    (htt : t ≠ t')
    (h0 : A l = .jz r lx l1) (h1 : A l1 = .dec r l2) (h2 : A l2 = .inc t l3)
    (h3 : A l3 = .inc t' l) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ), v r = k → (∀ s, v s ≤ B) → v t + v r ≤ B → v t' + v r ≤ B →
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update (Function.update (Function.update v r 0) t (v t + v r)) t'
        (v t' + v r), none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v hk hv _ _
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    have e : Function.update (Function.update (Function.update v r 0) t (v t + v r)) t'
        (v t' + v r) = v := by upd_tac
    rw [e]
    simp only [astep, h0, hk, ↓reduceIte]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v hk hv hb hb'
    have hr := hv r
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h0, hk, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h1], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h1, hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    have b1 := register_update_le _ r _ _ hv (show k ≤ B by omega)
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h2], b1⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h2]
    have b2 := register_update_le _ t _ _ b1 (show Function.update v r k t + 1 ≤ B by
      simp [Ne.symm hrt]; omega)
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h3], b2⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h3]
    have b3 := register_update_le _ t' _ _ b2 (show Function.update (Function.update v r k) t
        (Function.update v r k t + 1) t' + 1 ≤ B by
      simp [Ne.symm hrt', Ne.symm htt]; omega)
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ (by simp [hrt, hrt']) b3
      (by simp [hrt, hrt', htt, Ne.symm htt, Ne.symm hrt, Ne.symm hrt']; omega)
      (by simp [hrt, hrt', Ne.symm htt, Ne.symm hrt, Ne.symm hrt']; omega)) ?_
    congr 2
    upd_tac

/-- **Moving a register doubled**: the loop
`l: jz r lx l₁; l₁: dec r l₂; l₂: inc t l₃; l₃: inc t l` adds `2r` to `t` and clears `r`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the value of `r`: each round moves one unit twice. -/
theorem dmove_run {l lx l1 l2 l3 : Λ} {r t : Fin m} (hrt : r ≠ t)
    (h0 : A l = .jz r lx l1) (h1 : A l1 = .dec r l2) (h2 : A l2 = .inc t l3)
    (h3 : A l3 = .inc t l) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ), v r = k → (∀ s, v s ≤ B) → v t + 2 * v r ≤ B →
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update (Function.update v r 0) t (v t + 2 * v r), none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v hk hv _
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    have e : Function.update (Function.update v r 0) t (v t + 2 * v r) = v := by upd_tac
    rw [e]
    simp only [astep, h0, hk, ↓reduceIte]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v hk hv hb
    have hr := hv r
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h0, hk, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h1], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h1, hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    have b1 := register_update_le _ r _ _ hv (show k ≤ B by omega)
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h2], b1⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h2]
    have b2 := register_update_le _ t _ _ b1 (show Function.update v r k t + 1 ≤ B by
      simp [Ne.symm hrt]; omega)
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h3], b2⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h3]
    have b3 := register_update_le _ t _ _ b2 (show Function.update (Function.update v r k) t
        (Function.update v r k t + 1) t + 1 ≤ B by
      simp [Ne.symm hrt]; omega)
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ (by simp [hrt]) b3 (by simp [hrt, Ne.symm hrt]; omega)) ?_
    congr 2
    upd_tac

/-- **Subtracting a register**: the loop `l: jz q lx l₁; l₁: dec q l₂; l₂: dec r l`
subtracts `q` from `r` (truncated) and clears `q`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the value of `q`: each round removes one unit. -/
theorem sub_run {l lx l1 l2 : Λ} {q r : Fin m} (hqr : q ≠ r)
    (h0 : A l = .jz q lx l1) (h1 : A l1 = .dec q l2) (h2 : A l2 = .dec r l) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ), v q = k → (∀ s, v s ≤ B) →
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update (Function.update v q 0) r (v r - v q), none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v hk hv
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    have e : Function.update (Function.update v q 0) r (v r - v q) = v := by upd_tac
    rw [e]
    simp only [astep, h0, hk, ↓reduceIte]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v hk hv
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h0, hk, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h1], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h1, hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    have b1 := register_update_le _ q _ _ hv (show k ≤ B by have := hv q; omega)
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h2], b1⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h2]
    have b2 := register_update_le _ r _ _ b1 (show Function.update v q k r - 1 ≤ B by
      simp [Ne.symm hqr]; have := hv r; omega)
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ (by simp [hqr]) b2) ?_
    congr 2
    upd_tac

/-- **Halving a register as often as a counter says**: the loop
`l: jz c lx l₁; l₁: dec c l₂; l₂: half r l` divides `r` by `2 ^ c` and clears `c`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the value of `c`: `⌊⌊r / 2⌋ / 2 ^ k⌋ = ⌊r / 2 ^ (k + 1)⌋`. -/
theorem halve_run {l lx l1 l2 : Λ} {c r : Fin m} (hcr : c ≠ r)
    (h0 : A l = .jz c lx l1) (h1 : A l1 = .dec c l2) (h2 : A l2 = .half r l) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ), v c = k → (∀ s, v s ≤ B) →
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update (Function.update v c 0) r (v r / 2 ^ v c), none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v hk hv
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    have e : Function.update (Function.update v c 0) r (v r / 2 ^ v c) = v := by upd_tac
    rw [e]
    simp only [astep, h0, hk, ↓reduceIte]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v hk hv
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h0], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h0, hk, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h1], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h1, hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    have hb1 : ∀ s, Function.update v c k s ≤ B :=
      register_update_le _ _ _ _ hv (show k ≤ B by have := hv c; omega)
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, h2], hb1⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, h2]
    have hb2 : ∀ s, Function.update (Function.update v c k) r (Function.update v c k r / 2) s
        ≤ B := by
      intro s
      by_cases hs : s = r
      · subst hs; simp [Ne.symm hcr]; exact (Nat.div_le_self _ _).trans (hv _)
      · simp only [Function.update_of_ne hs]; exact hb1 s
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ (by simp [hcr]) hb2) ?_
    congr 2
    funext s
    by_cases hs : s = r
    · subst hs
      simp [hcr, Ne.symm hcr, Nat.div_div_eq_div_mul, pow_succ, mul_comm]
    · by_cases hs' : s = c
      · subst hs'; simp [hs]
      · simp [hs, hs']

/-- **Copying a register through a scratch register**: the loops
`l: jz src l₄ l₁; l₁: dec src l₂; l₂: inc dst l₃; l₃: inc z l` and
`l₄: jz z lx l₅; l₅: dec z l₆; l₆: inc src l₄`, with `z` clear, add `src` to `dst` and leave
everything else unchanged.

**Proof sketch.** `move2_run` moves `src` into `dst` and `z`, `move_run` moves `z` back. -/
theorem copy_run {l l1 l2 l3 l4 l5 l6 lx : Λ} {src dst z : Fin m} (h1 : src ≠ dst)
    (h2 : src ≠ z) (h3 : dst ≠ z)
    (a0 : A l = .jz src l4 l1) (a1 : A l1 = .dec src l2) (a2 : A l2 = .inc dst l3)
    (a3 : A l3 = .inc z l) (a4 : A l4 = .jz z lx l5) (a5 : A l5 = .dec z l6)
    (a6 : A l6 = .inc src l4)
    (v : Fin m → ℕ) (hz : v z = 0) (hv : ∀ s, v s ≤ B) (hb : v dst + v src ≤ B) :
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update v dst (v dst + v src), none) := by
  refine (move2_run h1 h2 h3 a0 a1 a2 a3 _ v rfl hv hb (by have := hv src; omega)).trans ?_
  have b1 := register_update_le _ z _ _
    (register_update_le _ dst _ _ (register_update_le _ src _ _ hv (Nat.zero_le B)) hb)
    (show v z + v src ≤ B by have := hv src; omega)
  refine reach_of_eq (move_run (Ne.symm h2) a4 a5 a6 _ _ rfl b1
    (by simp [h1, h2, hz]; exact hv src)) ?_
  congr 2
  upd_tac

/-- **Shifting a register left as often as a counter says**: the loops
`l: jz c lx l₁; l₁: dec c l₂`, then `l₂ … l₅` moving `r` doubled into `z` (exit `l₆`), then
`l₆ … l₈` moving `z` back into `r` (exit `l`), with `z` clear, multiply `r` by `2 ^ c` and
clear `c`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the value of `c`: each round doubles `r` (`dmove_run`,
`move_run`). -/
theorem shl_run {l l1 l2 l3 l4 l5 l6 l7 l8 lx : Λ} {c r z : Fin m} (hcr : c ≠ r) (hcz : c ≠ z)
    (hrz : r ≠ z)
    (a0 : A l = .jz c lx l1) (a1 : A l1 = .dec c l2) (a2 : A l2 = .jz r l6 l3)
    (a3 : A l3 = .dec r l4) (a4 : A l4 = .inc z l5) (a5 : A l5 = .inc z l2)
    (a6 : A l6 = .jz z l l7) (a7 : A l7 = .dec z l8) (a8 : A l8 = .inc r l6) :
    ∀ (k : ℕ) (v : Fin m → ℕ), v c = k → v z = 0 → (∀ s, v s ≤ B) → v r * 2 ^ v c ≤ B →
    AReach A oracle x (GuardLe A x B) (some l, v, none)
      (some lx, Function.update (Function.update v c 0) r (v r * 2 ^ v c), none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v hk _ hv _
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, a0], hv⟩ ?_
    have e : Function.update (Function.update v c 0) r (v r * 2 ^ v c) = v := by
      funext s
      by_cases hs : s = r
      · subst hs; simp [hk]
      · by_cases hs' : s = c
        · subst hs'; simp [hs, hk]
        · simp [hs, hs']
    rw [e]
    simp only [astep, a0, hk, ↓reduceIte]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v hk hz hv hb
    have h2 : 2 * v r ≤ B := by
      rw [hk, pow_succ] at hb
      have : 2 ≤ 2 ^ k * 2 := by have := Nat.one_le_two_pow (n := k); omega
      calc 2 * v r ≤ v r * (2 ^ k * 2) := by rw [mul_comm]; exact Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ this
        _ ≤ B := hb
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, a0], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, a0, hk, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, ↓reduceIte]
    refine AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, a1], hv⟩ ?_
    simp only [astep, a1, hk, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    have hv1 : ∀ s, Function.update v c k s ≤ B :=
      register_update_le _ _ _ _ hv (show k ≤ B by have := hv c; omega)
    refine (dmove_run hrz a2 a3 a4 a5 _ _ rfl hv1
      (by simp [Ne.symm hcz, Ne.symm hcr, hz]; omega)).trans ?_
    have hv2 := register_update_le _ z _ _ (register_update_le _ r _ _ hv1 (Nat.zero_le B))
      (show Function.update v c k z + 2 * Function.update v c k r ≤ B by
        simp [Ne.symm hcz, Ne.symm hcr, hz]; omega)
    refine (move_run (Ne.symm hrz) a6 a7 a8 _ _ rfl hv2
      (by simp [hrz, Ne.symm hcz, Ne.symm hcr, hz]; omega)).trans ?_
    have hv3 : ∀ s, Function.update (Function.update (Function.update (Function.update
        (Function.update v c k) r 0) z (Function.update v c k z + 2 * Function.update v c k r))
        z 0) r (Function.update (Function.update (Function.update v c k) r 0) z
        (Function.update v c k z + 2 * Function.update v c k r) r +
        Function.update (Function.update (Function.update v c k) r 0) z
        (Function.update v c k z + 2 * Function.update v c k r) z) s ≤ B :=
      register_update_le _ _ _ _ (register_update_le _ _ _ _ hv2 (Nat.zero_le B)) (by
        simp [hrz, Ne.symm hcz, Ne.symm hcr, hz]; omega)
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ (by simp [hcr, hcz]) (by simp [hrz, Ne.symm hrz]) hv3 ?_) ?_
    · simp [hcr, hcz, hrz, Ne.symm hcz, Ne.symm hcr, hz]
      rw [hk, pow_succ] at hb
      calc 2 * v r * 2 ^ k = v r * (2 ^ k * 2) := by ring
        _ ≤ B := hb
    · congr 2
      funext s
      by_cases hs : s = r
      · subst hs
        simp [hcr, hcz, hrz, Ne.symm hcz, Ne.symm hcr, hz, pow_succ]; ring
      · by_cases hs' : s = c
        · subst hs'; simp [hs, hcz]
        · by_cases hs'' : s = z
          · subst hs''; simp [hs, hs', hz]
          · simp [hs, hs', hs'']

end Complexity.LogProg
```

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi

import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.ARMProof
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SpaceClasses

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Abstract register machines with wide registers

`Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides` turns a correct abstract register machine whose registers
hold `O(log |x|)` binary digits, calling logspace deciders, into a logspace decider. The run
and space theorem behind it (`Complexity.LogProg.arm_space`) allows any register width `W`;
only the wrapper fixes `W = O(log n)`. This file gives the wrappers for wider registers: a
general one (`Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_space`, into `SPACE S`), and the polynomial-width
and `S`-width forms consumed by polynomial-space and Savitch-type arguments.

This is infrastructure — the register-machine description of space-bounded algorithms of
[AB09, §4.1] extended to `S(n) ≥ log n` registers — not itself a result of the book.

## Main definitions

* none (wrapper theorems for `Complexity.LogProg.ARM`).

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_space` — the general wrapper: registers of `W(|x|)` binary
  digits, deciders using space `s_j`, both `O(S(|x|))` on the relevant lengths, give `SPACE S`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_SPACE` — registers of `O(S(|x|))` binary digits with
  logspace deciders, for `S ≥ logSpace`, give `SPACE S`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_pspace` — registers of polynomially many binary digits with
  `PSPACE` deciders give `PSPACE`; `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_pspace_of_logspace` and
  `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_pspace_val` are its logspace-decider and value-bound forms.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1, Definitions 4.1 and 4.5.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

open Turing

variable {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type}

/-- **Abstract register machines with registers of `W(|x|)` binary digits decide languages in
`SPACE S`** (general width): if, on every input `x`, the abstract machine `A`, calling
deciders for the languages `As j` that run in space `s j`, answers `x ∈ L` through
configurations meeting the syntactic preconditions with every register value of at most
`W |x|` binary digits (counting one increment), and both the register width and the
deciders' space on every virtual input a call can form (of length at most
`2|x| + 2 + m (2 W |x| + 2)`, `Complexity.LogProg.length_callSegs_le`) are at most
`C · S |x|`, with `S ≥ 1`, then `L ∈ SPACE S`. Infrastructure for [AB09, §4.1]; at
`S = W = O(logSpace)` it is `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides`.

**Proof sketch.** As for `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides`: collect the deciders in a clean
bank (`Complexity.LogProg.bank_cleanRun`); the virtual inputs are short
(`Complexity.LogProg.length_callSegs_le`), so the deciders' head ranges are at most
`B = C · S |x| + 1`; `Complexity.LogProg.arm_space` then gives a machine answering `x ∈ L`
within `m (W + 2) + k_D (2B + 1) ≤ (m C + 2m + k_D (2C + 3)) · S |x|` cells. -/
theorem arm_decides_space {L : Language Bool} [Fintype Λ] [DecidableEq Λ] (A : ARM m d Λ)
    (l₀ : Λ) (As : Fin d → Language Bool) (s : Fin d → ℕ → ℕ)
    (hAs : ∀ j, ∃ M : FinTM Bool, M.DecidesInSpace (As j) (s j))
    (S W : ℕ → ℕ) (C : ℕ) (hS : ∀ n, 1 ≤ S n) (hW : ∀ n, W n ≤ C * S n)
    (hs : ∀ j n v, v ≤ 2 * n + 2 + m * (2 * W n + 2) → s j v ≤ C * S n)
    (hcorr : ∀ x, AHalt A (fun j V => MultiTapeTM.indicator (As j : Set (List Bool)) V) x
      (fun a => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ r, (Nat.bits (a.2.1 r + 1)).length ≤ W x.length)
      (some l₀, fun _ => 0, none) (MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x)) :
    L ∈ SPACE S := by
  classical
  let Ms : Fin d → FinTM Bool := fun j => Classical.choose (hAs j)
  have hMs : ∀ j, (Ms j).DecidesInSpace (As j) (s j) := fun j => Classical.choose_spec (hAs j)
  set kD := bankK Ms + bankK Ms with hkD
  set oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool :=
    fun j V => MultiTapeTM.indicator (As j : Set (List Bool)) V with horacle
  refine ⟨m * C + 2 * m + kD * (2 * C + 3),
    compileFinTM (armProg A l₀) (l₀, .start) (bankTM Ms) (bankStart Ms), fun x => ?_⟩
  set n := x.length with hn
  have hS1 := hS n
  set B := C * S n + 1 with hB
  obtain ⟨N, h1, h2, hm⟩ := hcorr x
  -- the preconditions of `arm_space`: syntactic ones, clean decider runs within `B`
  have hpre : ∀ t < N, Pre A oracle (bankTM Ms) (bankStart Ms) B x
      (arun A oracle x (some l₀, fun _ => 0, none) t) ∧
      ∀ r, ((Nat.bits ((arun A oracle x (some l₀, fun _ => 0, none) t).2.1 r + 1)).length : ℤ)
        ≤ ((W n : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
    intro t ht
    obtain ⟨hps, hbd⟩ := hm t ht
    refine ⟨?_, fun r => by exact_mod_cast hbd r⟩
    generalize hat : arun A oracle x (some l₀, fun _ => 0, none) t = a at hps hbd
    rcases a with ⟨_ | l, v, res⟩
    · trivial
    · simp only [Pre]
      cases hA : A l with
      | jeq r s' l₁ l₀' => simpa [PreS, hA] using hps
      | jeqIn r l₁ l₀' => simpa [PreS, hA] using hps
      | jeqFst r l₁ l₀' => simpa [PreS, hA] using hps
      | jeqSnd r l₁ l₀' => simpa [PreS, hA] using hps
      | inc => trivial
      | dec => trivial
      | clr => trivial
      | half => trivial
      | jz => trivial
      | jodd => trivial
      | ret => trivial
      | valP => trivial
      | valQ => trivial
      | call j md args l₁ l₀' =>
      simp only [PreS, hA] at hps
      refine ⟨hps, ?_⟩
      refine cleanRun_mono (bank_cleanRun Ms As s hMs j _) ?_
      have hVl := length_callSegs_le (x := x) ⟨j, md, args, l₁, l₀'⟩ (W n)
        (fun r => Nat.bits (v r))
        (fun r => by
          show (Nat.bits (v r)).length ≤ W n
          have h0 : (Nat.bits (v r + 1)).length ≤ W n := hbd r
          have hle : (Nat.bits (v r)).length ≤ (Nat.bits (v r + 1)).length :=
            length_bits_mono (by omega)
          omega) hps
      have := hs j n _ hVl
      simp only [hB]
      exact max_le (by omega) (by omega)
  obtain ⟨T, hT, hsp⟩ := arm_space A l₀ oracle (bankTM Ms) (bankStart Ms) B (W n) N
    (MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x) h1 h2 hpre
  refine ⟨T, hT, hsp.trans ?_⟩
  -- the arithmetic: `m (W + 2) + k_D (2B + 1) ≤ (m C + 2m + k_D (2C + 3)) S`
  show _ ≤ (m * C + 2 * m + kD * (2 * C + 3)) * S n
  have f0 : m * W n ≤ m * (C * S n) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left m (hW n)
  have e1 : m * (W n + 2) = m * W n + 2 * m := by ring
  have e2 : kD * (2 * B + 1) = 2 * kD * C * S n + 3 * kD := by simp only [hB]; ring
  have e3 : (m * C + 2 * m + kD * (2 * C + 3)) * S n =
      m * (C * S n) + 2 * m * S n + 2 * kD * C * S n + 3 * kD * S n := by ring
  rw [e1, e2, e3]
  have f1 : 2 * m ≤ 2 * m * S n := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
  have f2 : 3 * kD ≤ 3 * kD * S n := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
  omega

/-- **Abstract register machines with `O(S)`-digit registers and logspace subroutines decide
languages in `SPACE S`**: for `S ≥ logSpace`, if on every input `x` the abstract machine `A`,
calling deciders for languages in `L`, answers `x ∈ L` through configurations meeting the
syntactic preconditions with every register value of at most `K · S |x|` binary digits
(counting one increment), then `L ∈ SPACE S`. Infrastructure for [AB09, §4.1]
(`S(n) ≥ log n`, the book's standing convention, p. 79); no monotonicity or constructibility
of `S` is needed.

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_space` with `W = K · S`. A virtual input
has length `v ≤ 2|x| + 2 + m (2 K S + 2) ≤ A · 2^S` (as `|x| < 2^{logSpace |x|} ≤ 2^S` and
`S < 2^S`), so a logspace decider uses `c · logSpace v ≤ c (A + 1) · S` cells
(`Complexity.logSpace_le_of_le_mul_two_pow`). -/
theorem arm_decides_SPACE {L : Language Bool} [Fintype Λ] [DecidableEq Λ] (A : ARM m d Λ)
    (l₀ : Λ) (As : Fin d → Language Bool) (hAs : ∀ j, As j ∈ LOGSPACE) (S : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hS : ∀ n, logSpace n ≤ S n) (K : ℕ)
    (hcorr : ∀ x, AHalt A (fun j V => MultiTapeTM.indicator (As j : Set (List Bool)) V) x
      (fun a => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ r, (Nat.bits (a.2.1 r + 1)).length ≤ K * S x.length)
      (some l₀, fun _ => 0, none) (MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x)) :
    L ∈ SPACE S := by
  classical
  have hc : ∀ j, ∃ (c : ℕ) (M : FinTM Bool), M.DecidesInSpace (As j) fun n => c * logSpace n :=
    fun j => hAs j
  let c : Fin d → ℕ := fun j => Classical.choose (hc j)
  have hc' : ∀ j, ∃ M : FinTM Bool, M.DecidesInSpace (As j) fun n => c j * logSpace n :=
    fun j => Classical.choose_spec (hc j)
  set cs := ∑ j, c j with hcs
  have hcj : ∀ j, c j ≤ cs := fun j =>
    Finset.single_le_sum (f := c) (fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _) (Finset.mem_univ j)
  set A₀ := 2 + 2 * m + 2 * m * K with hA₀
  have hS1 : ∀ n, 1 ≤ S n := fun n => le_trans (by simp [logSpace]) (hS n)
  refine arm_decides_space A l₀ As (fun j n => c j * logSpace n) hc' S (fun n => K * S n)
    (K + cs * (A₀ + 1)) hS1 (fun n => Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.le_add_right _ _))
    (fun j n v hv => ?_) hcorr
  -- a virtual input has length at most `A₀ · 2^S`
  set P := 2 ^ S n with hP
  have hnP : n + 1 ≤ P :=
    (succ_le_two_pow_log n).trans (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (hS n))
  have hSP : S n ≤ P := (Nat.lt_two_pow_self).le
  have hvP : v ≤ A₀ * P := by
    have g1 : m * K * S n ≤ m * K * P := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ hSP
    have g2 : m ≤ m * P := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
    have e1 : m * (2 * (K * S n) + 2) = 2 * (m * K * S n) + 2 * m := by ring
    have e2 : A₀ * P = 2 * P + 2 * (m * P) + 2 * (m * K * P) := by simp only [hA₀]; ring
    rw [e1] at hv; rw [e2]; omega
  have hlog := logSpace_le_of_le_mul_two_pow hvP (hS1 n)
  calc c j * logSpace v ≤ cs * ((A₀ + 1) * S n) := Nat.mul_le_mul (hcj j) hlog
    _ = cs * (A₀ + 1) * S n := by ring
    _ ≤ (K + cs * (A₀ + 1)) * S n := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.le_add_left _ _)

/-- **Abstract register machines with polynomially wide registers decide languages in
`PSPACE`**: if, on every input `x`, the abstract machine `A`, calling deciders for languages
in `PSPACE`, answers `x ∈ L` through configurations meeting the syntactic preconditions with
every register value of at most `C₀ (|x| + 1)^{c₀}` binary digits (counting one increment),
then `L ∈ PSPACE`. Infrastructure for [AB09, §4.1, Definition 4.5].

**Proof sketch.** Each decider `j` runs in space `c_j (n^{e_j} + 1)`. A virtual input has
length `v ≤ A (|x| + 1)^{c₀ + 1}`, so decider `j` uses at most
`c_j (A^{e_j} + 1) (|x| + 1)^{(c₀ + 1) e_j}` cells. With `E = (c₀ + 1)(Σ e_j + 1)`,
`Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_space` at `S = (n + 1)^E` gives `L ∈ SPACE ((n + 1)^E)`,
inside `PSPACE` (`Complexity.SPACE_succ_pow_subset_PSPACE`). -/
theorem arm_decides_pspace {L : Language Bool} [Fintype Λ] [DecidableEq Λ] (A : ARM m d Λ)
    (l₀ : Λ) (As : Fin d → Language Bool) (hAs : ∀ j, As j ∈ PSPACE) (C₀ c₀ : ℕ)
    (hcorr : ∀ x, AHalt A (fun j V => MultiTapeTM.indicator (As j : Set (List Bool)) V) x
      (fun a => PreS A x a ∧
        ∀ r, (Nat.bits (a.2.1 r + 1)).length ≤ C₀ * (x.length + 1) ^ c₀)
      (some l₀, fun _ => 0, none) (MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x)) :
    L ∈ PSPACE := by
  classical
  have hc : ∀ j, ∃ (e c : ℕ) (M : FinTM Bool),
      M.DecidesInSpace (As j) fun n => c * (n ^ e + 1) := fun j => by
    obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion.mp (hAs j)
    exact ⟨e, he⟩
  let e : Fin d → ℕ := fun j => Classical.choose (hc j)
  let c : Fin d → ℕ := fun j => Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec (hc j))
  have hc' : ∀ j, ∃ M : FinTM Bool, M.DecidesInSpace (As j) fun n => c j * (n ^ e j + 1) :=
    fun j => Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec (hc j))
  set A₀ := 2 + 2 * m + 2 * m * C₀ with hA₀
  set es := ∑ j, e j with hes
  set E := (c₀ + 1) * (es + 1) with hE
  set C := C₀ + ∑ j, c j * (A₀ ^ e j + 1) with hC
  have hej : ∀ j, e j ≤ es := fun j =>
    Finset.single_le_sum (f := e) (fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _) (Finset.mem_univ j)
  have hcj : ∀ j, c j * (A₀ ^ e j + 1) ≤ C := fun j =>
    (Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun j => c j * (A₀ ^ e j + 1)) (fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _)
      (Finset.mem_univ j)).trans (Nat.le_add_left _ _)
  have hc₀E : c₀ + 1 ≤ E := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
  have hpowE : ∀ n k, k ≤ E → (n + 1) ^ k ≤ (n + 1) ^ E := fun n k hk =>
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) hk
  refine SPACE_succ_pow_subset_PSPACE E (arm_decides_space A l₀ As
    (fun j n => c j * (n ^ e j + 1)) hc' (fun n => (n + 1) ^ E) (fun n => C₀ * (n + 1) ^ c₀) C
    (fun n => Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by omega))
    (fun n => Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.le_add_right _ _) (hpowE n c₀ (by omega)))
    (fun j n v hv => ?_) hcorr)
  -- a virtual input has length at most `A₀ (n + 1)^{c₀ + 1}`
  set P := (n + 1) ^ (c₀ + 1) with hP
  have hP1 : n + 1 ≤ P := by
    simpa using Nat.pow_le_pow_right (show 0 < n + 1 by omega) (show 1 ≤ c₀ + 1 by omega)
  have hPc : (n + 1) ^ c₀ ≤ P := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
  have hvP : v ≤ A₀ * P := by
    have g1 : m * C₀ * (n + 1) ^ c₀ ≤ m * C₀ * P := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ hPc
    have g2 : m ≤ m * P := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (by omega)
    have e1 : m * (2 * (C₀ * (n + 1) ^ c₀) + 2) = 2 * (m * C₀ * (n + 1) ^ c₀) + 2 * m := by
      ring
    have e2 : A₀ * P = 2 * P + 2 * (m * P) + 2 * (m * C₀ * P) := by simp only [hA₀]; ring
    rw [e1] at hv; rw [e2]; omega
  -- decider `j` uses at most `c_j (A₀^{e_j} + 1) (n + 1)^E` cells
  have hpow : v ^ e j + 1 ≤ (A₀ ^ e j + 1) * (n + 1) ^ E := by
    have h1 : v ^ e j ≤ A₀ ^ e j * (n + 1) ^ E := by
      calc v ^ e j ≤ (A₀ * P) ^ e j := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hvP _
        _ = A₀ ^ e j * (n + 1) ^ ((c₀ + 1) * e j) := by rw [mul_pow, hP, ← pow_mul]
        _ ≤ A₀ ^ e j * (n + 1) ^ E := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (hpowE n _
          (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ ((hej j).trans (Nat.le_succ _))))
    have h2 : 1 ≤ (n + 1) ^ E := Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by omega)
    rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul]; omega
  calc c j * (v ^ e j + 1) ≤ c j * ((A₀ ^ e j + 1) * (n + 1) ^ E) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ hpow
    _ = c j * (A₀ ^ e j + 1) * (n + 1) ^ E := by ring
    _ ≤ C * (n + 1) ^ E := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (hcj j)

/-- **Polynomially wide registers with logspace subroutines give `PSPACE`**: the form of
`Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_pspace` with deciders in `L`. Infrastructure for [AB09, §4.1].

**Proof sketch.** `L ⊆ PSPACE` (`Complexity.LOGSPACE_subset_PSPACE`). -/
theorem arm_decides_pspace_of_logspace {L : Language Bool} [Fintype Λ] [DecidableEq Λ]
    (A : ARM m d Λ) (l₀ : Λ) (As : Fin d → Language Bool) (hAs : ∀ j, As j ∈ LOGSPACE)
    (C₀ c₀ : ℕ)
    (hcorr : ∀ x, AHalt A (fun j V => MultiTapeTM.indicator (As j : Set (List Bool)) V) x
      (fun a => PreS A x a ∧
        ∀ r, (Nat.bits (a.2.1 r + 1)).length ≤ C₀ * (x.length + 1) ^ c₀)
      (some l₀, fun _ => 0, none) (MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x)) :
    L ∈ PSPACE :=
  arm_decides_pspace A l₀ As (fun j => LOGSPACE_subset_PSPACE (hAs j)) C₀ c₀ hcorr

/-- **Exponentially large register values give `PSPACE`**: the form of
`Complexity.LogProg.arm_decides_pspace` with register values at most
`2^{C₀ (|x| + 1)^{c₀}}`. Infrastructure for [AB09, §4.1].

**Proof sketch.** A value `v ≤ 2^N` has `v + 1 < 2^{N + 2}`, so `|bits (v + 1)| ≤ N + 2
≤ (C₀ + 2)(|x| + 1)^{c₀}` (`Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_le`). -/
theorem arm_decides_pspace_val {L : Language Bool} [Fintype Λ] [DecidableEq Λ]
    (A : ARM m d Λ) (l₀ : Λ) (As : Fin d → Language Bool) (hAs : ∀ j, As j ∈ PSPACE)
    (C₀ c₀ : ℕ)
    (hcorr : ∀ x, AHalt A (fun j V => MultiTapeTM.indicator (As j : Set (List Bool)) V) x
      (fun a => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ r, a.2.1 r ≤ 2 ^ (C₀ * (x.length + 1) ^ c₀))
      (some l₀, fun _ => 0, none) (MultiTapeTM.indicator (L : Set (List Bool)) x)) :
    L ∈ PSPACE := by
  refine arm_decides_pspace A l₀ As hAs (C₀ + 2) c₀ fun x =>
    (hcorr x).mono fun a ⟨h1, h2⟩ => ⟨h1, fun r => ?_⟩
  set N := C₀ * (x.length + 1) ^ c₀ with hN
  have h3 := length_bits_succ_le ((h2 r).trans (Nat.le_succ _))
  have h4 : 2 ≤ 2 * (x.length + 1) ^ c₀ :=
    Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (Nat.one_le_pow _ _ (by omega))
  have e : (C₀ + 2) * (x.length + 1) ^ c₀ = N + 2 * (x.length + 1) ^ c₀ := by
    simp only [hN]; ring
  omega

end Complexity.LogProg
```

```
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.DblLang

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Random access to a general input in logarithmic space

A logspace machine reads its input at a position held in binary on a work tape [AB09, §4.1:
"a pointer into the input"]. The received `LogProg` layer has no such access for a general
(non-unary) input: the input instructions of `Complexity.LogProg.ARM` presuppose inputs
`⟨1ⁿ, w⟩` or `⟨1ⁿ, ⟨u, w⟩⟩`, and a call's virtual input is the whole input or its leading run
of `1`s followed by register words (P0 reception audit, `audits/ch34-p0-findings.md`). This
file supplies the missing piece twice, at the two levels later logspace programs use:

* **as a program fragment**: `Complexity.LogProg.readIn_run` reads bit `i` of the input,
  `i` held in binary on a register, into the control state (a counter register stepped up to
  `i` in lockstep with the input head, the received equality, increment, rewind and clear
  fragments), and restores everything else;
* **as a language pair**: `Complexity.implicitlyLogspaceComputable_id` — the bit and length
  languages of the identity, `Complexity.inputBitLang` and `Complexity.inputLenLang`, are in
  `L` — so an abstract register machine reads its own input at a register-held position by a
  `whole`-mode call with that register as its one argument (`Complexity.LogProg.vword_whole₁`,
  `Complexity.indicator_indexLang_pairEncode`).

Phase P4.4b of `AroraBarakChapters3-4Plan.md` (the B7 statement mini-phase, recorded in
`audits/ch4-p44-resolutions-addendum.md`). The fragment is campaign-owned and lives here,
not in `Machines/`, by decision D3; it is built only from received fragments.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.RdPh`, `Complexity.LogProg.readTr` — the phases and the transition
  table of the input-read fragment.
* `Complexity.inputBitLang`, `Complexity.inputLenLang` — `{⟨u, i⟩ | uᵢ = 1}` and
  `{⟨u, i⟩ | i < |u|}`.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.vword_whole₁` — a `whole` call with one argument presents `⟨u, V r⟩`.
* `Complexity.indicator_indexLang_pairEncode` — the answer of an `indexLang` decider on a
  genuine pair.
* `Complexity.pairEncode_ne_nil` — no pair is empty (so `[]` lies in no `indexLang`).
* `Complexity.pairEncode_getD` — a shared bit-address formula for doubled fields,
  separators, and suffixes of paired inputs.
* `Complexity.LogProg.alignedPair_loop` — a bounded ARM pair scan at any positive stride.
* `Complexity.LogProg.register_update_le` — the shared register-bound update rule.
* `Complexity.LogProg.registerCopy_loop` — copy by bounded counting, preserving the source.
* `Complexity.LogProg.registerScale_loop` — consume a source into a scaled destination.
* `Complexity.LogProg.canonicalTail_loop` — canonical-tail and width validation before decoding.
* `Complexity.LogProg.boundedDecode_loop` — reverse binary decoding after the width check, the
  unit-stride case of `Complexity.LogProg.boundedDecodeStride_loop`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.arm_chain` — a bounded chain of increments or decrements of one register.
* `Complexity.LogProg.access_width_half`, `Complexity.LogProg.drop_canon` — halving removes one
  binary digit; the tail loop's flag is `Canon`.
* `Complexity.indicator_inputBitLang`, `Complexity.indicator_inputLenLang` — the answers of the
  bit and length languages on a genuine pair.
* `Complexity.pairEncode_getD_snd` — a letter of the second field of a pair.
* `Complexity.LogProg.indexedSeek_loop` — bounded positioning within a strided segment.
* `Complexity.LogProg.inputLength_loop` — a bounded ARM loop counting a general input
  through its length-query oracle.
* `Complexity.LogProg.readIn_run` — the input-read fragment (proved; phase-P4.4b
  statement).
* `Complexity.implicitlyLogspaceComputable_id` — input random access in `L` (proved;
  phase-P4.4b statement), with `Complexity.inputBitLang_mem`, `Complexity.inputLenLang_mem`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1; §4.3, Definition 4.16.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- No pair encoding is the empty word: `pairEncode x y` contains the separator. -/
theorem pairEncode_ne_nil (x y : List Bool) : pairEncode x y ≠ [] := by
  intro h
  have := congrArg List.length h
  simp [length_pairEncode] at this

/-- **The answer of an index-language decider on a genuine pair**: the indicator of
`indexLang p` at `⟨u, bits v⟩` is the decision of `p u v`. -/
theorem indicator_indexLang_pairEncode (p : List Bool → ℕ → Prop) (u : List Bool) (v : ℕ) :
    MultiTapeTM.indicator (indexLang p : Set (List Bool)) (pairEncode u (Nat.bits v)) =
      @decide (p u v) (Classical.dec _) := by
  rw [LogProg.indicator_eq_decide]
  exact decide_eq_decide.mpr (pairEncode_mem_indexLang p u v)

namespace LogProg

/-- **A `whole`-mode call with one argument** presents the pair of the whole input and the
argument register's word: its virtual input is `⟨u, V r⟩`. -/
theorem vword_whole₁ {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (u : List Bool) (j : Fin d) (r : Fin m) (l₁ l₀ : Λ)
    (V : Fin m → List Bool) :
    vword (callSegs ⟨j, .whole, [r], l₁, l₀⟩ u V) = pairEncode u (V r) := by
  simp [callSegs, Mode.seg0, argSegs, vword, render, pairEncode_eq_dbl]

/-! ## The input-read fragment -/

/-- The phases of the input-read fragment: the equality test of the counter with the index
(`eC`, `eBy`, `eBn`), the read (`yes`) or advance (`no`) step, the counter increment (`iC`,
`iB`), and, carrying the symbol read, the input rewind (`rw₁`, `rw₂`) and the counter clear
(`cR`, `cE`). -/
inductive RdPh where
  | eC | eBy | eBn
  | yes | no
  | iC | iB
  | rw₁ (a : Option Bool) | rw₂ (a : Option Bool)
  | cR (a : Option Bool) | cE (a : Option Bool)
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

variable {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} {x : List Bool}

/-- **The transition table of the input-read fragment** on index register `r` and counter
register `s`, its phases embedded by `st` and its exits by `ex`. With the input head on
position `k + 1` (input symbol `k`) and the counter holding `bits k`: compare the counter with
the index (`eq_run`); if equal, take the symbol under the head; if not, stop at the right
blank, or else step the input head right and increment the counter (`inc_run`). Then rewind
the input head to position `1` (`rewind_x`) and clear the counter (`clr_run`), exiting into
`ex a` with the symbol `a` taken. -/
def readTr (r s : Fin m) (st : RdPh → Λ) (ex : Option Bool → Λ) :
    RdPh → Option Bool → (Fin m → Option Bool) → Action m Bool Λ
  | .eC, _, w => eqCAct s r (st .eC) (st .eBy) (st .eBn) (w s) (w r)
  | .eBy, _, w => eqBAct s r (st .eBy) (st .yes) (w s)
  | .eBn, _, w => eqBAct s r (st .eBn) (st .no) (w s)
  | .yes, a, _ => goAct (st (.rw₁ a))
  | .no, a, _ =>
    match a with
    | none => goAct (st (.rw₁ none))
    | some _ => xAct s 1 0 (st .iC)
  | .iC, _, w => incCAct s (st .iC) (st .iB) (w s)
  | .iB, _, w => incBAct s (st .iB) (st .eC) (w s)
  | .rw₁ a, _, _ => xAct s (-1) 0 (st (.rw₂ a))
  | .rw₂ a, b, _ => rw2Act s (st (.rw₂ a)) (st (.cR a)) b
  | .cR a, _, w => toEndAct s (st (.cR a)) (st (.cE a)) (w s)
  | .cE a, _, w => clrEAct s (st (.cE a)) (ex a) (w s)

/-- A proof-only instance of the frozen read table, with disjoint phase and exit labels.
Exits halt, which lets the received fragments' non-call trace clauses recover phase
membership before the final exit. The eventual transport does not require `st` injective. -/
private def readModel (r s : Fin m) : RProg m 0 (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) :=
  ⟨⟨.inl .eC, fun l a w => match l with
    | .inl ph => readTr r s Sum.inl Sum.inr ph a w
    | .inr _ => junkAct⟩, fun _ => none⟩

/-- A read-fragment boundary with its input position and canonical counter explicit. -/
private def readAt (c : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x) (s : Fin m)
    (l : RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) (ip : Fin (x.length + 2)) (k : ℕ) :
    Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x :=
  ⟨some l, ip, Function.update c.workTapes s (FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits k)),
    Function.update c.workTapePos s 0, c.output⟩

/-- The frame and head-range assertion, before restricting the control label to a phase. -/
private def readFrame (c : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x) (r s : Fin m)
    (d : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x) : Prop :=
  ∃ l ip f p q, d = ⟨some l, ip, Function.update c.workTapes s f,
      Function.update (Function.update c.workTapePos s p) r q, c.output⟩ ∧
    -1 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ (Nat.bits (x.length + 1)).length ∧
    -1 ≤ q ∧ q ≤ (Nat.bits (x.length + 1)).length

/-- A counter-only fragment view satisfies the frame. -/
private theorem readFrame_reg (c : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x) (r s : Fin m)
    (hrs : r ≠ s) (hrp : c.workTapePos r = 0) (l l' : RdPh ⊕ Option Bool)
    (ip : Fin (x.length + 2)) (k : ℕ) (f : ℤ → Option Bool) (p : ℤ)
    (hp : -1 ≤ p) (hp' : p ≤ (Nat.bits (x.length + 1)).length) :
    readFrame c r s (regCfg (readAt c s l ip k) l' s f p) := by
  refine ⟨l', ip, f, p, 0, ?_, hp, hp', by omega, by omega⟩
  refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ ?_ rfl
  · simp [regCfg, readAt]
  · simp [regCfg, readAt, Function.update_of_ne hrs, hrp]

/-- A boundary configuration is framed with both active heads at the origin. -/
private theorem readFrame_at (c : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x) (r s : Fin m)
    (hrs : r ≠ s) (hrp : c.workTapePos r = 0) (l : RdPh ⊕ Option Bool)
    (ip : Fin (x.length + 2)) (k : ℕ) : readFrame c r s (readAt c s l ip k) := by
  have he : regCfg (readAt c s l ip k) l s (FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits k)) 0 =
      readAt c s l ip k := by simp [regCfg, readAt]
  rw [← he]
  exact readFrame_reg c r s hrs hrp l l ip k _ 0 (by omega) (by omega)

/-- The comparison fragment is framed, with its common head position bounded by the
counter word rather than by the possibly much longer index word.

**Proof sketch.** Apply the received equality fragment with the counter as its first
register. Its trace moves the two heads together, so the counter length bounds both;
rewrite its configuration view into the frame and use monotonicity of binary length. -/
private theorem read_eq (c : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x) (r s : Fin m)
    (hrs : r ≠ s) (i k : ℕ) (hr : c.workTapes r = FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits i))
    (hrp : c.workTapePos r = 0) (hk : k ≤ x.length)
    (ip : Fin (x.length + 2)) :
    ∃ T, rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) (readAt c s (.inl .eC) ip k) T =
        readAt c s (.inl (if k = i then .yes else .no)) ip k ∧
      ∀ n < T, readFrame c r s
        (rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) (readAt c s (.inl .eC) ip k) n) := by
  obtain ⟨T, he, hm⟩ := eq_run (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) s r (Ne.symm hrs)
    (.inl .eC) (.inl .eBy) (.inl .eBn) (.inl .yes) (.inl .no)
    (fun _ _ => rfl) (fun _ _ => rfl) (fun _ _ => rfl) rfl rfl rfl
    (readAt c s (.inl .eC) ip k) k i (by simp [readAt])
    (by simp [readAt, hrs, hr])
  have view (l : RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) :
      eqCfg (readAt c s (.inl .eC) ip k) l s r 0 = readAt c s l ip k := by
    simp [eqCfg, readAt, Function.update_of_ne hrs, hrp]
  rw [view, view] at he
  refine ⟨T, ?_, fun n hn => ?_⟩
  · simpa only [apply_ite Sum.inl] using he
  · rw [view] at hm
    obtain ⟨l, p, he', _, hlo, hhi⟩ := hm n hn
    refine ⟨l, ip, FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits k), p, p, ?_, hlo, ?_, hlo, ?_⟩
    · rw [he']; simp [eqCfg, readAt]
    all_goals
      have hw := length_bits_mono (show k ≤ x.length + 1 by omega)
      omega

/-- One ordinary model step applies the frozen table. -/
private theorem read_one (c : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x) (r s : Fin m)
    (ph : RdPh) (ip : Fin (x.length + 2)) (k : ℕ) :
    rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) (readAt c s (.inl ph) ip k) 1 =
      (readTr r s Sum.inl Sum.inr ph (inSym x ip.val)
        (readAt c s (.inl ph) ip k).workTapeSymbols).apply (readAt c s (.inl ph) ip k) := by
  rw [rrun_one, rstep_noncall (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) _ (.inl ph) rfl rfl]
  simp only [MultiTapeTM.step, readModel, readAt, inputSymbol_eq, inSym]

/-- Rewind and clear restore the boundary input head and the empty counter.

**Proof sketch.** Invoke `rewind_x` at the current input position, then `clr_run` on the
counter. Both leave the index tape and all unrelated tapes unchanged. -/
private theorem read_cleanup (c : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x) (r s : Fin m)
    (hrs : r ≠ s) (hrp : c.workTapePos r = 0) (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ x.length)
    (ip : Fin (x.length + 2)) (a : Option Bool) :
    ∃ T, rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) (readAt c s (.inl (.rw₁ a)) ip k) T =
        readAt c s (.inr a) 1 0 ∧
      ∀ n < T, readFrame c r s
        (rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) (readAt c s (.inl (.rw₁ a)) ip k) n) := by
  obtain ⟨A, heA, hmA⟩ := rewind_x (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0)
    (readAt c s (.inl (.rw₁ a)) ip k) s 0 (.inl (.rw₁ a)) (.inl (.rw₂ a)) (.inl (.cR a))
    (fun _ _ => rfl) (fun _ _ => rfl) rfl rfl ip
  have xv (l : RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) (jp : Fin (x.length + 2)) :
      xCfg (readAt c s (.inl (.rw₁ a)) ip k) l jp s 0 = readAt c s l jp k := by
    simp [xCfg, readAt]
  rw [xv, xv] at heA
  have hone : (⟨1, by omega⟩ : Fin (x.length + 2)) = 1 := by
    apply Fin.ext; simp
  rw [hone] at heA
  obtain ⟨B, heB, hmB⟩ := clr_run (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) s
    (.inl (.cR a)) (.inl (.cE a)) (.inr a)
    (fun _ _ => rfl) (fun _ _ => rfl) rfl rfl (readAt c s (.inl (.cR a)) 1 k) k
  have rv (l : RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) (j : ℕ) :
      regCfg (readAt c s (.inl (.cR a)) 1 k) l s (FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits j)) 0 =
      readAt c s l 1 j := by simp [regCfg, readAt]
  rw [rv, rv] at heB
  refine ⟨A + B, by rw [rrun_add, heA, heB], fun n hn => ?_⟩
  by_cases hnA : n < A
  · rw [xv] at hmA
    obtain ⟨l, jp, he, _⟩ := hmA n hnA
    rw [he, xv]
    exact readFrame_at c r s hrs hrp l jp k
  · have hn' : n = A + (n - A) := by omega
    rw [hn', rrun_add, heA]
    rw [rv] at hmB
    obtain ⟨l, f, p, he, _, hlo, hhi⟩ := hmB (n - A) (by omega)
    rw [he]
    exact readFrame_reg c r s hrs hrp _ l 1 k f p hlo
      (hhi.trans (by exact_mod_cast length_bits_mono (show k ≤ x.length + 1 by omega)))

/-- Advance one counter/input position when both the requested index and the input end
are still ahead.

**Proof sketch.** The received equality fragment answers no. One table step advances the
input head, and the received increment fragment advances the counter. -/
private theorem read_advance (c : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x) (r s : Fin m)
    (hrs : r ≠ s) (i k : ℕ) (hr : c.workTapes r = FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits i))
    (hrp : c.workTapePos r = 0) (hk : k < min i x.length) :
    ∃ T, rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0)
        (readAt c s (.inl .eC) ⟨k + 1, by omega⟩ k) T =
        readAt c s (.inl .eC) ⟨k + 2, by omega⟩ (k + 1) ∧
      ∀ n < T, readFrame c r s (rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0)
        (readAt c s (.inl .eC) ⟨k + 1, by omega⟩ k) n) := by
  obtain ⟨A, heA, hmA⟩ := read_eq c r s hrs i k hr hrp (by omega) ⟨k + 1, by omega⟩
  rw [if_neg (show k ≠ i by omega)] at heA
  have he1 : rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0)
      (readAt c s (.inl .no) ⟨k + 1, by omega⟩ k) 1 =
      readAt c s (.inl .iC) ⟨k + 2, by omega⟩ k := by
    rw [read_one, inSym_succ, List.getElem?_eq_getElem (show k < x.length by omega)]
    simp only [readTr]
    refine Cfg.ext rfl ?_ ?_ ?_ (by simp [Action.apply, xAct, readAt])
    · apply Fin.ext
      simpa only [Action.apply, xAct, readAt] using
        (moveInputPos_pos_val (x := x) ⟨k + 1, by omega⟩ (by dsimp; omega))
    · funext j z; simp [Action.apply, xAct, readAt]
    · funext j; simp [Action.apply, xAct, readAt]
  obtain ⟨B, heB, hmB⟩ := inc_run (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) s
    (.inl .iC) (.inl .iB) (.inl .eC) (fun _ _ => rfl) (fun _ _ => rfl) rfl rfl
    (readAt c s (.inl .iC) ⟨k + 2, by omega⟩ k) k
  have rv (l : RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) (j : ℕ) :
      regCfg (readAt c s (.inl .iC) ⟨k + 2, by omega⟩ k) l s (FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits j)) 0 =
      readAt c s l ⟨k + 2, by omega⟩ j := by simp [regCfg, readAt]
  rw [rv, rv] at heB
  refine ⟨A + (1 + B), by rw [rrun_add, heA, rrun_add, he1, heB], fun n hn => ?_⟩
  by_cases hnA : n < A
  · exact hmA n hnA
  · have hn' : n = A + (n - A) := by omega
    rw [hn', rrun_add, heA]
    by_cases heq : n - A = 0
    · rw [heq, rrun_zero]
      exact readFrame_at c r s hrs hrp _ _ _
    · have hn'' : n - A = 1 + (n - A - 1) := by omega
      rw [hn'', rrun_add, he1]
      rw [rv] at hmB
      obtain ⟨l, f, p, he, _, hlo, hhi⟩ := hmB (n - A - 1) (by omega)
      rw [he]
      exact readFrame_reg c r s hrs hrp _ l _ k f p hlo
        (hhi.trans (by exact_mod_cast length_bits_mono (show k + 1 ≤ x.length + 1 by omega)))

/-- At the smaller of the desired index and input length, read the answer and clean up.

**Proof sketch.** Equality selects the requested cell when the index is reached; otherwise
this is the right blank and the requested answer is also `none`. Rewind and clear complete
the routine. -/
private theorem read_finish (c : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x) (r s : Fin m)
    (hrs : r ≠ s) (i : ℕ) (hr : c.workTapes r = FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits i))
    (hrp : c.workTapePos r = 0) :
    ∃ T, rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0)
        (readAt c s (.inl .eC) ⟨min i x.length + 1, by omega⟩ (min i x.length)) T =
        readAt c s (.inr x[i]?) 1 0 ∧
      ∀ n < T, readFrame c r s (rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0)
        (readAt c s (.inl .eC) ⟨min i x.length + 1, by omega⟩ (min i x.length)) n) := by
  let k := min i x.length
  let ip : Fin (x.length + 2) := ⟨k + 1, by dsimp [k]; omega⟩
  obtain ⟨A, heA, hmA⟩ := read_eq c r s hrs i k hr hrp (by dsimp [k]; omega) ip
  have he1 : rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0)
      (readAt c s (.inl (if k = i then .yes else .no)) ip k) 1 =
      readAt c s (.inl (.rw₁ x[i]?)) ip k := by
    by_cases hki : k = i
    · rw [if_pos hki, read_one]
      have hin : inSym x ip.val = x[i]? := by dsimp [ip]; rw [inSym_succ, hki]
      rw [hin]
      simp [readTr, goAct, Action.apply, readAt]
    · have hklen : k = x.length := by dsimp [k] at *; omega
      have hi : x.length ≤ i := by dsimp [k] at *; omega
      rw [if_neg hki, read_one]
      have hin : inSym x ip.val = none := by dsimp [ip]; rw [inSym_succ, hklen]; simp
      rw [hin, List.getElem?_eq_none hi]
      simp [readTr, goAct, Action.apply, readAt]
  obtain ⟨B, heB, hmB⟩ := read_cleanup c r s hrs hrp k (by dsimp [k]; omega) ip x[i]?
  refine ⟨A + (1 + B), by rw [rrun_add, heA, rrun_add, he1, heB], fun n hn => ?_⟩
  by_cases hnA : n < A
  · exact hmA n hnA
  · have hn' : n = A + (n - A) := by omega
    rw [hn', rrun_add, heA]
    by_cases heq : n - A = 0
    · rw [heq, rrun_zero]
      exact readFrame_at c r s hrs hrp _ _ _
    · have hn'' : n - A = 1 + (n - A - 1) := by omega
      rw [hn'', rrun_add, he1]
      exact hmB (n - A - 1) (by omega)

/-- The proof-only model executes the whole routine with the original frame.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the counter up to `min i |x|`, concatenate each bounded advance,
then append `read_finish`. All sub-runs come from the received fragments. -/
private theorem read_model_run (c : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x) (r s : Fin m)
    (hrs : r ≠ s) (i : ℕ) (hr : c.workTapes r = FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits i))
    (hrp : c.workTapePos r = 0) :
    ∃ T, rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) (readAt c s (.inl .eC) 1 0) T =
        readAt c s (.inr x[i]?) 1 0 ∧
      ∀ n < T, readFrame c r s
        (rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) (readAt c s (.inl .eC) 1 0) n) := by
  have rounds : ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≤ min i x.length), ∃ T,
      rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) (readAt c s (.inl .eC) 1 0) T =
        readAt c s (.inl .eC) ⟨k + 1, by omega⟩ k ∧
      ∀ n < T, readFrame c r s
        (rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) (readAt c s (.inl .eC) 1 0) n) := by
    intro k
    induction k with
    | zero => intro hk; exact ⟨0, rfl, fun n hn => by omega⟩
    | succ k ih =>
      intro hk
      obtain ⟨A, heA, hmA⟩ := ih (by omega)
      obtain ⟨B, heB, hmB⟩ := read_advance c r s hrs i k hr hrp (by omega)
      refine ⟨A + B, by rw [rrun_add, heA, heB], fun n hn => ?_⟩
      by_cases hnA : n < A
      · exact hmA n hnA
      · have hn' : n = A + (n - A) := by omega
        rw [hn', rrun_add, heA]
        exact hmB (n - A) (by omega)
  obtain ⟨A, heA, hmA⟩ := rounds (min i x.length) le_rfl
  obtain ⟨B, heB, hmB⟩ := read_finish c r s hrs i hr hrp
  refine ⟨A + B, by rw [rrun_add, heA, heB], fun n hn => ?_⟩
  by_cases hnA : n < A
  · exact hmA n hnA
  · have hn' : n = A + (n - A) := by omega
    rw [hn', rrun_add, heA]
    exact hmB (n - A) (by omega)

/-- The proof-only model has no calls, so its register run is its ordinary machine run. -/
private theorem read_run_eq (r s : Fin m) (c : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x) (n : ℕ) :
    rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) c n = (readModel r s).tm.runFrom c n := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ n ih =>
    rw [rrun_succ, ih, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step']
    cases hs : ((readModel r s).tm.runFrom c n).state <;>
      simp [rstep, MultiTapeTM.step, hs, readModel]

/-- Every state strictly before an exit in the proof-only model is a fragment phase.

**Proof sketch.** The final exit is live. Earlier configurations are live because halts are
absorbing. An earlier exit would halt on its next step, contradicting that liveness. -/
private theorem read_model_phase (r s : Fin m) (c : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x)
    (T : ℕ) (a : Option Bool)
    (hT : (rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) c T).state = some (.inr a)) :
    ∀ n < T, ∃ ph, (rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) c n).state = some (.inl ph) := by
  simp only [read_run_eq] at hT ⊢
  have hl := (readModel r s).tm.runFrom_state_ne_none_of_le c T
    (by rw [hT]; simp)
  intro n hn
  cases he : ((readModel r s).tm.runFrom c n).state with
  | none => exact (hl n (by omega) he).elim
  | some l =>
    cases l with
    | inl ph => exact ⟨ph, rfl⟩
    | inr b =>
      exfalso
      apply hl (n + 1) (by omega)
      rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step']
      simp [MultiTapeTM.step, he, readModel, junkAct, Action.apply]

/-- The frozen table commutes with replacing its phase and exit labels. -/
private theorem read_action_map (r s : Fin m) (st : RdPh → Λ) (ex : Option Bool → Λ)
    (ph : RdPh) (a : Option Bool) (w : Fin m → Option Bool) :
    (readTr r s Sum.inl Sum.inr ph a w).mapState (Sum.elim st ex) = readTr r s st ex ph a w := by
  cases ph <;>
    simp [readTr, eqCAct, eqBAct, incCAct, incBAct, rw2Act, toEndAct, clrEAct,
      regAct, mv2Act, xAct, goAct, Action.mapState, apply_ite] <;>
    repeat' first | split | rfl

section Read

variable (P : RProg m d Λ) (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (r s : Fin m) (hrs : r ≠ s)
  (st : RdPh → Λ) (ex : Option Bool → Λ)
  (htr : ∀ ph a w, P.tm.tr (st ph) a w = readTr r s st ex ph a w)
  (hc : ∀ ph, P.call (st ph) = none)

include hrs htr hc in
/-- **The input-read fragment** (phase P4.4b; proved): from phase `eC`, with
`bits i` on the index register `r`, an empty counter register `s`, both heads on cell `0` and
the input head on position `1`, the program reaches the exit `ex x[i]?` — symbol `i` of the
input, `none` when `i ≥ |x|` — in the same configuration otherwise (registers, heads, input
position and output restored). Throughout, only registers `s` and `r` change (the tape of `s`,
the heads of both), both heads stay in `[-1, |bits (|x| + 1)|]`, and every state is an
ordinary fragment state: the fragment's space is these two ranges, independently of `i`.
A hand-built fragment: no received layer reads a general input at a register-held position
(the `Parse` fragments assume unary-first inputs).

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the counter value `k ≤ min i |x|`, the input head on position
`k + 1`. `eq_run` (with `r₁ := s`, so both heads stay within `|bits k|`) compares `bits k`
with `bits i`. If `k = i`, phase `yes` takes `inSym x (i + 1) = x[i]?`. Otherwise phase `no`
reads `inSym x (k + 1)`: at the right blank (`k = |x| < i`) the symbol taken is
`none = x[i]?`; on a letter (`k < |x|`) the head steps right and `inc_run` turns `bits k` into
`bits (k + 1)`, `k + 1 ≤ |x|`. Then `rewind_x` returns the input head to position `1`, and
`clr_run` empties the counter (its head within `|bits k|`). -/
theorem readIn_run (c : Cfg m Bool Λ x) (i : ℕ)
    (hr : c.workTapes r = FinTM.bufferTape (Nat.bits i)) (hs : c.workTapes s = FinTM.bufferTape [])
    (hrp : c.workTapePos r = 0) (hsp : c.workTapePos s = 0) (hip : c.inputPos.val = 1) :
    ∃ T, rrun P oracle { c with state := some (st .eC) } T = { c with state := some (ex x[i]?) } ∧
      ∀ t < T, ∃ (ph : RdPh) (ip : Fin (x.length + 2)) (f : ℤ → Option Bool) (q q' : ℤ),
        rrun P oracle { c with state := some (st .eC) } t =
          ⟨some (st ph), ip, Function.update c.workTapes s f,
            Function.update (Function.update c.workTapePos s q) r q', c.output⟩ ∧
        -1 ≤ q ∧ q ≤ (Nat.bits (x.length + 1)).length ∧
        -1 ≤ q' ∧ q' ≤ (Nat.bits (x.length + 1)).length := by
  let c₀ : Cfg m Bool (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) x :=
    ⟨some (.inl .eC), c.inputPos, c.workTapes, c.workTapePos, c.output⟩
  let d₀ := readAt c₀ s (.inl .eC) 1 0
  let rename : (RdPh ⊕ Option Bool) → Λ := Sum.elim st ex
  obtain ⟨T, hT, hmid⟩ := read_model_run c₀ r s hrs i hr hrp
  have hphase := read_model_phase r s d₀ T x[i]? (by rw [hT]; rfl)
  have hm : ∀ n ≤ T, rrun P oracle (d₀.mapState rename) n =
      (rrun (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) d₀ n).mapState rename := by
    intro n
    induction n with
    | zero => intro _; rfl
    | succ n ih =>
      intro hn
      obtain ⟨ph, hph⟩ := hphase n (by omega)
      rw [rrun_succ, ih (by omega), rrun_succ]
      rw [rstep_noncall P oracle _ (st ph) (by simp [Cfg.mapState, hph, rename]) (hc ph),
        rstep_noncall (readModel r s) (fun j => j.elim0) _ (.inl ph) hph rfl]
      simp only [MultiTapeTM.step, Cfg.mapState, hph, Option.map_some, rename, Sum.elim_inl]
      rw [htr]
      rw [← read_action_map]
      rfl
  have hstart : d₀.mapState rename = {c with state := some (st .eC)} := by
    refine Cfg.ext rfl ?_ ?_ ?_ rfl
    · apply Fin.ext; simpa [d₀, c₀, readAt, Cfg.mapState] using hip.symm
    · simp [d₀, c₀, readAt, Cfg.mapState, Nat.zero_bits, ← hs, Function.update_eq_self]
    · simp [d₀, c₀, readAt, Cfg.mapState, ← hsp, Function.update_eq_self]
  rw [← hstart]
  refine ⟨T, ?_, fun n hn => ?_⟩
  · rw [hm T le_rfl, hT]
    refine Cfg.ext rfl ?_ ?_ ?_ rfl
    · apply Fin.ext; simpa [readAt, Cfg.mapState] using hip.symm
    · simp [readAt, c₀, Cfg.mapState, Nat.zero_bits, ← hs, Function.update_eq_self]
    · simp [readAt, c₀, Cfg.mapState, ← hsp, Function.update_eq_self]
  · obtain ⟨ph, hph⟩ := hphase n hn
    obtain ⟨l, ip, f, p, q, he, hlo, hhi, hlo', hhi'⟩ := hmid n hn
    have hl : l = Sum.inl ph := by rw [he] at hph; exact Option.some.inj hph
    subst l
    refine ⟨ph, ip, f, p, q, ?_, hlo, hhi, hlo', hhi'⟩
    rw [hm n (by omega), he]
    rfl

end Read

end LogProg

/-! ## Input access as a language pair -/

/-- The bit language of the identity: `{⟨u, bits i⟩ | uᵢ = 1}` (`0`-based; `false` beyond the
end). -/
def inputBitLang : Language Bool := indexLang fun u i => u.getD i false = true

/-- The length language of the identity: `{⟨u, bits i⟩ | i < |u|}`. -/
def inputLenLang : Language Bool := indexLang fun u i => i < u.length

/-- **The bit language answers with the indexed letter**: on a genuine pair `⟨y, bits a⟩` the
indicator of `Complexity.inputBitLang` is letter `a` of `y` (`false` beyond the end).

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.indicator_indexLang_pairEncode`, by cases on the letter. -/
theorem indicator_inputBitLang (y : List Bool) (a : ℕ) :
    MultiTapeTM.indicator (inputBitLang : Set (List Bool)) (pairEncode y (Nat.bits a)) =
      y.getD a false := by
  rw [inputBitLang, indicator_indexLang_pairEncode]
  cases y.getD a false <;> simp

/-- **The length language answers with the comparison**: on a genuine pair `⟨y, bits a⟩` the
indicator of `Complexity.inputLenLang` decides `a < |y|`.

**Proof sketch.** `Complexity.indicator_indexLang_pairEncode`. -/
theorem indicator_inputLenLang (y : List Bool) (a : ℕ) :
    MultiTapeTM.indicator (inputLenLang : Set (List Bool)) (pairEncode y (Nat.bits a)) =
      decide (a < y.length) := by
  rw [inputLenLang, indicator_indexLang_pairEncode]
  exact decide_eq_decide.mpr Iff.rfl

/-- Reading a paired word by position selects a doubled first-field bit, a separator bit,
or a suffix bit. The default is `false` beyond the complete word. This common address rule
serves the nested layouts of index dropping, query reshaping, and multiplication.

**Proof sketch.** Within the first field, write the address as twice its quotient by two
plus its parity and cite `getElem?_dbl`. Outside that field, the append lookup rule exposes
the separator or the suffix. -/
theorem pairEncode_getD (u v : List Bool) (j : ℕ) :
    (pairEncode u v).getD j false =
      if j < 2 * u.length then u.getD (j / 2) false
      else if j = 2 * u.length then false
      else if j = 2 * u.length + 1 then true
      else v.getD (j - 2 * u.length - 2) false := by
  by_cases hj : j < 2 * u.length
  · rw [if_pos hj, pairEncode_eq_dbl, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD,
      List.append_assoc, List.getElem?_append_left (by simpa using hj)]
    have hc : j / 2 < u.length := by omega
    have hread : (dbl u)[j]? = some u[j / 2] := by
      rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one j with h | h
      · have he : 2 * (j / 2) + (false : Bool).toNat = j := by simp; omega
        simpa only [he] using getElem?_dbl u (j / 2) hc false
      · have he : 2 * (j / 2) + (true : Bool).toNat = j := by simp; omega
        simpa only [he] using getElem?_dbl u (j / 2) hc true
    rw [hread]
    simp [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, hc]
  · rw [if_neg hj, pairEncode_eq_dbl, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD,
      List.append_assoc, List.getElem?_append_right (by simp; omega)]
    simp only [length_dbl]
    by_cases he : j = 2 * u.length
    · subst j; simp
    · rw [if_neg he]
      by_cases he' : j = 2 * u.length + 1
      · subst j; simp
      · rw [if_neg he', show j - 2 * u.length = (j - 2 * u.length - 2) + 1 + 1 by omega]
        rfl

/-- **A letter of the second field of a pair**: letter `j` of `v` sits at position
`2 |u| + 2 + j` of `⟨u, v⟩` (reading with default `false`, also beyond the end).

**Proof sketch.** The address lies past the doubled first field and the separator, so the last
case of `pairEncode_getD` reads letter `j` of `v`. -/
theorem pairEncode_getD_snd (u v : List Bool) (j : ℕ) :
    (pairEncode u v).getD (2 * u.length + 2 + j) false = v.getD j false := by
  rw [pairEncode_getD, if_neg (by omega), if_neg (by omega), if_neg (by omega)]
  congr 1
  omega

namespace LogProg

open Classical

/-- A length-query/increment loop counts the host input, with all registers bounded by
the chosen bound. The oracle law is needed only up to the first failing query, at the
input length. This shared ARM fragment is used by the query validators.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the input length minus the current counter. Below the end,
the length call succeeds and increment reduces the remaining count. At the end, the call
fails and exits. The counter never exceeds the input length; all other registers stay
unchanged. Both instructions meet the received ARM syntactic preconditions. -/
theorem inputLength_loop {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (A : ARM m d Λ)
    (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (x : List Bool) (r : Fin m) (j : Fin d)
    (scan inc done : Λ)
    (hscan : A scan = .call j .whole [r] inc done)
    (hinc : A inc = .inc r scan)
    (hquery : ∀ n ≤ x.length, oracle j (pairEncode x (Nat.bits n)) = decide (n < x.length))
    (B : ℕ) (hB : x.length ≤ B) (v : Fin m → ℕ)
    (hv : ∀ s, v s ≤ B) (hr : v r ≤ x.length) :
    AReach A oracle x (fun a => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ s, a.2.1 s ≤ B)
      (some scan, v, none) (some done, Function.update v r x.length, none) := by
  generalize hN : x.length - v r = N
  induction N using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing v with
  | h N ih =>
    have hs : astep A oracle x (some scan, v, none) =
        (some (if v r < x.length then inc else done), v, none) := by
      simp only [astep, hscan, vword_whole₁, hquery (v r) hr, decide_eq_true_eq]
    have hg : PreS A x (some scan, v, none) ∧ ∀ s, v s ≤ B :=
      ⟨by simp [PreS, hscan], hv⟩
    by_cases hlt : v r < x.length
    · let v' := Function.update v r (v r + 1)
      have hv' : ∀ s, v' s ≤ B := by
        intro s
        by_cases he : s = r
        · subst s; dsimp [v']; rw [Function.update_self]; omega
        · simpa [v', Function.update_of_ne he] using hv s
      have hr' : v' r ≤ x.length := by simp [v']; omega
      have hremain : x.length - v' r < N := by simp [v']; omega
      have hc := ih (x.length - v' r) hremain v' hv' hr' rfl
      have hi : astep A oracle x (some inc, v, none) = (some scan, v', none) := by
        simp [astep, hinc, v']
      apply AReach.step hg
      rw [hs, if_pos hlt]
      apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, hinc], hv⟩
      rw [hi]
      simpa only [v', Function.update_idem] using hc
    · have he : v r = x.length := by omega
      have hp := AReach.single (A := A) (oracle := oracle) (x := x)
        (G := fun a => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ s, a.2.1 s ≤ B) (a := (some scan, v, none)) hg
      have hs' : astep A oracle x (some scan, v, none) = (some done, v, none) := by
        rw [hs, if_neg hlt]
      have hvdone : Function.update v r x.length = v := by
        rw [← he, Function.update_eq_self]
      rw [hvdone]
      simpa only [hs'] using hp

/-- **A bounded straight chain of unit steps of one register**: if the instructions at the
labels `labels 0, …, labels (k - 1)` all increment register `r` (`up = true`), or all decrement
it (`up = false`), each passing to the next label, then the run from `labels 0` reaches
`labels k` with `r` raised (respectively lowered) by `k`, every register staying at most `B`.
The side condition is `v r + k ≤ B` for increments and `k ≤ v r` for decrements, so that no
decrement truncates. The labels may belong to any larger ARM; no new reachability relation is
needed. The increment chains of the bounded fragments below and the codec's chains
(`Complexity.Codec.incChain`, `Complexity.Codec.decChain`) are its instances.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `k`. A step at `labels 0` moves `r` by one, within the bound;
the rest of the chain starts at `labels 1`. -/
theorem arm_chain {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (A : ARM m d Λ)
    (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (x : List Bool) (r : Fin m) (up : Bool)
    (labels : ℕ → Λ) (k B : ℕ)
    (hcode : ∀ i < k, A (labels i) =
      bif up then .inc r (labels (i + 1)) else .dec r (labels (i + 1)))
    (v : Fin m → ℕ) (hv : ∀ s, v s ≤ B) (hk : bif up then v r + k ≤ B else k ≤ v r) :
    AReach A oracle x (fun a => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ s, a.2.1 s ≤ B)
      (some (labels 0), v, none)
      (some (labels k), Function.update v r (bif up then v r + k else v r - k), none) := by
  induction k generalizing labels v with
  | zero =>
    have e : (bif up then v r + 0 else v r - 0) = v r := by cases up <;> rfl
    rw [e, Function.update_eq_self]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    have hc := hcode 0 (by omega)
    let v' := Function.update v r (bif up then v r + 1 else v r - 1)
    have hv' : ∀ s, v' s ≤ B := by
      intro s
      by_cases hs : s = r
      · subst s
        have := hv r
        cases up <;> simp only [cond_true, cond_false] at hk <;> simp [v'] <;> omega
      · simpa [v', Function.update_of_ne hs] using hv s
    have hpre : PreS A x (some (labels 0), v, none) := by cases up <;> simp [PreS, hc]
    have hstep : astep A oracle x (some (labels 0), v, none) = (some (labels 1), v', none) := by
      cases up <;> simp [astep, hc, v']
    have hp := ih (fun i => labels (i + 1)) (fun i hi => hcode (i + 1) (by omega)) v' hv'
      (by cases up <;> simp only [cond_true, cond_false, v', Function.update_self] at hk ⊢ <;>
        omega)
    have e : Function.update v' r (bif up then v' r + k else v' r - k) =
        Function.update v r (bif up then v r + (k + 1) else v r - (k + 1)) := by
      cases up <;> simp only [cond_true, cond_false, v', Function.update_self,
        Function.update_idem] <;> congr 1 <;> omega
    apply AReach.step ⟨hpre, hv⟩
    rw [hstep]
    rw [e] at hp
    exact hp

/-- A bounded straight sequence of register increments (`arm_chain` with `up = true`). The
labels may belong to any larger ARM; no new reachability relation is needed. -/
private lemma arm_increments {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (A : ARM m d Λ)
    (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (x : List Bool) (r : Fin m)
    (labels : ℕ → Λ) (k B : ℕ)
    (hcode : ∀ i < k, A (labels i) = .inc r (labels (i + 1)))
    (v : Fin m → ℕ) (hv : ∀ s, v s ≤ B) (hk : v r + k ≤ B) :
    AReach A oracle x (fun a => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ s, a.2.1 s ≤ B)
      (some (labels 0), v, none)
      (some (labels k), Function.update v r (v r + k), none) :=
  arm_chain A oracle x r true labels k B hcode v hv hk

/-- An aligned pair scan using the input-bit oracle, at any positive stride. It rejects
exactly failed pair decodes and otherwise leaves the pointer just beyond the separator.
The scan imposes no canonicality condition on either field. Four increment chains move
past a first `false`, a first `true`, an equal pair, or the separator respectively.

**Proof sketch.** Induct by two input letters. An empty word fails the first end test;
a singleton fails the second. Equal letters advance and recur, `01` exits at the payload,
and `10` rejects. Each advance is `arm_increments`; all pointer values stay below the
supplied end address. This is the shared aligned-scan argument for nested query layouts. -/
theorem alignedPair_loop {m d : ℕ} {Λ : Type} (A : ARM m d Λ)
    (oracle : Fin d → List Bool → Bool) (x : List Bool)
    (r limit : Fin m) (j : Fin d) (scan first : Λ) (test read : Bool → Λ)
    (fail done : Λ) (advance : Fin 4 → ℕ → Λ) (stride B : ℕ)
    (hstride : 0 < stride) (hrlimit : r ≠ limit)
    (hscan : A scan = .jeq r limit fail first)
    (hfirst : A first = .call j .whole [r] (advance 1 0) (advance 0 0))
    (htest : ∀ b, A (test b) = .jeq r limit fail (read b))
    (hread : ∀ b, A (read b) = .call j .whole [r]
      (if b then advance 2 0 else advance 3 0) (if b then fail else advance 2 0))
    (hadvance : ∀ k i, i < stride → A (advance k i) = .inc r (advance k (i + 1)))
    (hend : advance 0 stride = test false ∧ advance 1 stride = test true ∧
      advance 2 stride = scan ∧ advance 3 stride = done)
    (w : List Bool) (v : Fin m → ℕ) (hv : ∀ s, v s ≤ B)
    (hlimit : v limit = v r + stride * w.length)
    (horacle : ∀ i < w.length,
      oracle j (pairEncode x (Nat.bits (v r + stride * i))) = w.getD i false) :
    match pairDecode w with
    | none => ∃ t ≤ w.length,
        AReach A oracle x (fun a => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ s, a.2.1 s ≤ B)
          (some scan, v, none) (some fail, Function.update v r (v r + stride * t), none)
    | some (a, _) =>
        AReach A oracle x (fun a => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ s, a.2.1 s ≤ B)
          (some scan, v, none)
          (some done, Function.update v r (v r + stride * (2 * a.length + 2)), none) := by
  let G := fun a : AConf m Λ => PreS A x a ∧ ∀ s, a.2.1 s ≤ B
  have upd : ∀ (v : Fin m → ℕ) (q : ℕ), (∀ s, v s ≤ B) → q ≤ B →
      ∀ s, Function.update v r q s ≤ B := by
    intro v q hv hq s
    by_cases hs : s = r
    · subst s; simpa using hq
    · simpa [Function.update_of_ne hs] using hv s
  have initial : ∀ (b : Bool) (tail : List Bool) (v : Fin m → ℕ),
      (∀ s, v s ≤ B) → v limit = v r + stride * (b :: tail).length →
      oracle j (pairEncode x (Nat.bits (v r))) = b →
      AReach A oracle x G (some scan, v, none)
        (some (test b), Function.update v r (v r + stride), none) := by
    intro b tail v hv hl ho
    have hstep : v r + stride ≤ B := by
      have := hv limit
      have := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right stride (show 0 < (b :: tail).length by simp)
      omega
    have hne : v r ≠ v limit := by
      have := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right stride (show 0 < (b :: tail).length by simp)
      omega
    apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, hscan, hrlimit], hv⟩
    simp only [astep, hscan, if_neg hne]
    apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, hfirst], hv⟩
    simp only [astep, hfirst, vword_whole₁, ho]
    cases b
    · simpa only [Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte, hend.1] using
        arm_increments A oracle x r (advance 0) stride B (hadvance 0) v hv hstep
    · simpa only [↓reduceIte, hend.2.1] using
        arm_increments A oracle x r (advance 1) stride B (hadvance 1) v hv hstep
  induction w using List.twoStepInduction generalizing v with
  | nil =>
    simp only [pairDecode]
    refine ⟨0, by simp, ?_⟩
    have he : v r = v limit := by simpa using hlimit.symm
    simpa only [astep, hscan, if_pos he, Nat.mul_zero, Nat.add_zero,
      Function.update_eq_self] using
      (AReach.single (A := A) (oracle := oracle) (x := x) (G := G)
        (a := (some scan, v, none)) ⟨by simp [PreS, hscan, hrlimit], hv⟩)
  | singleton b =>
    have ho := horacle 0 (by simp)
    simp only [Nat.mul_zero, Nat.add_zero, List.getD_cons_zero] at ho
    have hi := initial b [] v hv hlimit ho
    let v' := Function.update v r (v r + stride)
    have hv' : ∀ s, v' s ≤ B := by
      apply upd v _ hv
      have := hv limit
      simp only [List.length_singleton, Nat.mul_one] at hlimit
      omega
    have he : v' r = v' limit := by simp [v', hrlimit.symm]; simpa using hlimit.symm
    have hp : AReach A oracle x G (some (test b), v', none) (some fail, v', none) := by
      simpa only [astep, htest, if_pos he] using
        (AReach.single (A := A) (oracle := oracle) (x := x) (G := G)
          (a := (some (test b), v', none)) ⟨by simp [PreS, htest, hrlimit], hv'⟩)
    cases b <;> simp only [pairDecode] <;>
      exact ⟨1, by simp, by simpa [Nat.mul_one] using hi.trans hp⟩
  | cons_cons b c tail ih _ =>
    have hb := horacle 0 (by simp)
    have hc := horacle 1 (by simp)
    simp only [Nat.mul_zero, Nat.add_zero, List.getD_cons_zero] at hb
    simp only [Nat.mul_one, List.getD_cons_succ, List.getD_cons_zero] at hc
    have hi := initial b (c :: tail) v hv hlimit hb
    let v' := Function.update v r (v r + stride)
    let v'' := Function.update v r (v r + 2 * stride)
    have hbound : v r + 2 * stride ≤ B := by
      have := hv limit
      simp only [List.length_cons, Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one] at hlimit
      omega
    have hv' : ∀ s, v' s ≤ B := upd v _ hv (by omega)
    have hv'' : ∀ s, v'' s ≤ B := upd v _ hv hbound
    have hne : v' r ≠ v' limit := by
      simp only [v', Function.update_self, Function.update_of_ne hrlimit.symm]
      simp only [List.length_cons, Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one] at hlimit
      omega
    have hcall : AReach A oracle x G (some (test b), v', none)
        (some (if c then (if b then advance 2 0 else advance 3 0)
          else (if b then fail else advance 2 0)), v', none) := by
      apply AReach.step ⟨by simp [PreS, htest, hrlimit], hv'⟩
      simp only [astep, htest, if_neg hne]
      have ho : oracle j (pairEncode x (Nat.bits (v' r))) = c := by simpa [v'] using hc
      simpa only [astep, hread, vword_whole₁, ho] using
        (AReach.single (A := A) (oracle := oracle) (x := x) (G := G)
          (a := (some (read b), v', none)) ⟨by simp [PreS, hread], hv'⟩)
    have hinc : ∀ k : Fin 4, AReach A oracle x G
        (some (advance k 0), v', none) (some (advance k stride), v'', none) := by
      intro k
      have hp := arm_increments A oracle x r (advance k) stride B (hadvance k) v' hv'
        (by simp [v']; omega)
      simpa only [v', v'', Function.update_self, Function.update_idem,
        show v r + stride + stride = v r + 2 * stride by omega] using hp
    have hnext : v'' limit = v'' r + stride * tail.length := by
      simp only [v'', Function.update_self, Function.update_of_ne hrlimit.symm]
      simp only [List.length_cons, Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one] at hlimit
      omega
    have honext : ∀ i < tail.length,
        oracle j (pairEncode x (Nat.bits (v'' r + stride * i))) = tail.getD i false := by
      intro i hi
      have hp := horacle (i + 2) (by simp; omega)
      simpa only [v'', Function.update_self, Nat.mul_add,
        show v r + (stride * i + stride * 2) = v r + 2 * stride + stride * i by omega,
```
