```
import Mathlib.Tactic.FinCases
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.NARMKit
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.PathWalk

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The nondeterministic walk machine for `PATH`

[AB09, §4.1.2]: the machine `Complexity.LogProg.pathA`, a nondeterministic abstract register
machine with nine registers and the two input-access deciders
(`Complexity.inputBitLang`, `Complexity.inputLenLang`): it checks the unary prefix and the
matrix shape, guesses `s` and `t` and checks them against the input, then walks from `s`,
guessing each next vertex and reading its matrix bit, for at most `n` steps. This file
defines the machine and its register file and proves the walk loop correct
(`Complexity.LogProg.ps_walk`) in the continuation semantics of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.NARMKit`; the input checks and the assembly are in
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Logspace.PathWalkProof`.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.PathLabel`, `Complexity.LogProg.pathA` — the machine.
* `Complexity.LogProg.pathAs`, `Complexity.LogProg.pathOr` — its deciders.
* `Complexity.LogProg.PReg` — its register file, by name; `Complexity.LogProg.PS` — the
  semantics at a label and register file.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.pathA_npreS` — the machine meets the syntactic preconditions.
* `Complexity.LogProg.ps_index` — the matrix position of an edge.
* `Complexity.LogProg.ps_walk` — the walk loop. [AB09, §4.1.2]

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.2.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

open Turing

set_option synthInstance.maxSize 4096 in
set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
/-- The labels of the walk machine: the unary scan (`u*`), the matrix scan (`m*`), the guess
and check of the source (`s*`) and of the target (`t*`), the walk (`w*`), the three
add-twice loops of the index computation (`ak k`, `ak₁ k`, `ak₂ k`, `ak₃ k`), and the two
answers. -/
inductive PathLabel
  | u0 | u1 | u2 | u3 | u4 | u5 | u6 | u7
  | m0 | mr | m1 | m2 | m3 | m4 | m5 | m7 | m8 | m9 | m10 | m11 | ms | m12
  | sg | sc | sm | scp | sbp | stt | sz1 | sz2 | sz3 | sz4 | sod | so1 | so2 | so3
  | se1 | se2 | se3 | sad | shf
  | tg | tc | tm | tcp | tbp | ttt | tend | tlen | tpar | tone | tzero | tad | thf
  | w0 | w1 | w2 | wg | wc | wm | wcp | wcb | wi1 | wi2 | wca | wrow | wrc | wrn | wcc
  | wrd | wcl | wcy | wby | wst
  | ak (k : Fin 3) | ak₁ (k : Fin 3) | ak₂ (k : Fin 3) | ak₃ (k : Fin 3)
  | acc | rej
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

open PathLabel

/-- The register added twice by add-twice loop `k`: `n`, `n`, the guessed vertex. -/
def akY : Fin 3 → Fin 9 := ![1, 1, 8]

/-- The exit of add-twice loop `k`. -/
def akEx : Fin 3 → PathLabel := ![wi1, wrn, wrd]

/-- **The walk machine** [AB09, §4.1.2]. Registers: `0` the input pointer `p`, `1` the vertex
count `n`, `2` and `3` counters `a`, `b`, `4` the source and then the current vertex, `5` the
target, `6` a scratch copy, `7` the step count, `8` the guessed next vertex. Deciders: `0`
reads an input bit, `1` compares with the input length.

* Unary scan: count the aligned `11` pairs into `n`, then expect `01`; `p = 2n + 2`.
* Matrix scan: aligned data pairs `00`/`11` counted by row `a` and column `b` (reset at `n`),
  inside the input; the separator `01` only after exactly `n²` pairs.
* Source and target: guess `s < n` (choose to stop or to increment), check the doubled field
  against the binary digits of `s` (parity and halving of a copy), then the separator;
  likewise `t < n` against the plain suffix, which must end the input.
* Walk: accept if the current vertex is `t`; reject after `n` steps; guess `v < n`, compute
  `p = 2n + 2 + 2(cur · n + v)` by add-twice loops, reject unless the input bit at `p` is `1`,
  move to `v`. -/
def pathA : NARM 9 2 PathLabel
  | u0 => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] u1 u2)
  | u1 => .det (.inc 0 u3)
  | u3 => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] u4 rej)
  | u4 => .det (.inc 0 u5)
  | u5 => .det (.inc 1 u0)
  | u2 => .det (.inc 0 u6)
  | u6 => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] u7 rej)
  | u7 => .det (.inc 0 m0)
  | m0 => .det (.call 1 .whole [0] mr rej)
  | mr => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] m1 m2)
  | m1 => .det (.inc 0 m3)
  | m3 => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] m5 rej)
  | m2 => .det (.inc 0 m4)
  | m4 => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] ms m5)
  | m5 => .det (.jeq 2 1 rej m7)
  | m7 => .det (.inc 0 m8)
  | m8 => .det (.inc 3 m9)
  | m9 => .det (.jeq 3 1 m10 m0)
  | m10 => .det (.clr 3 m11)
  | m11 => .det (.inc 2 m0)
  | ms => .det (.jeq 2 1 m12 rej)
  | m12 => .det (.inc 0 sg)
  | sg => .det (.jeq 4 1 rej sc)
  | sc => .choose scp sm
  | sm => .det (.inc 4 sg)
  | scp => .det (.jeq 6 4 stt sbp)
  | sbp => .det (.inc 6 scp)
  | stt => .det (.jz 6 sz1 sod)
  | sz1 => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] rej sz2)
  | sz2 => .det (.inc 0 sz3)
  | sz3 => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] sz4 rej)
  | sz4 => .det (.inc 0 tg)
  | sod => .det (.jodd 6 so1 se1)
  | so1 => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] so2 rej)
  | so2 => .det (.inc 0 so3)
  | so3 => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] sad rej)
  | se1 => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] rej se2)
  | se2 => .det (.inc 0 se3)
  | se3 => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] rej sad)
  | sad => .det (.inc 0 shf)
  | shf => .det (.half 6 stt)
  | tg => .det (.jeq 5 1 rej tc)
  | tc => .choose tcp tm
  | tm => .det (.inc 5 tg)
  | tcp => .det (.jeq 6 5 ttt tbp)
  | tbp => .det (.inc 6 tcp)
  | ttt => .det (.jz 6 tend tlen)
  | tend => .det (.call 1 .whole [0] rej w0)
  | tlen => .det (.call 1 .whole [0] tpar rej)
  | tpar => .det (.jodd 6 tone tzero)
  | tone => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] tad rej)
  | tzero => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] rej tad)
  | tad => .det (.inc 0 thf)
  | thf => .det (.half 6 ttt)
  | w0 => .det (.jeq 4 5 acc w1)
  | w1 => .det (.jeq 7 1 rej w2)
  | w2 => .det (.clr 8 wg)
  | wg => .det (.jeq 8 1 rej wc)
  | wc => .choose wcp wm
  | wm => .det (.inc 8 wg)
  | wcp => .det (.clr 0 wcb)
  | wcb => .det (.clr 3 (ak 0))
  | ak k => .det (.jeq 3 (akY k) (akEx k) (ak₁ k))
  | ak₁ k => .det (.inc 0 (ak₂ k))
  | ak₂ k => .det (.inc 0 (ak₃ k))
  | ak₃ k => .det (.inc 3 (ak k))
  | wi1 => .det (.inc 0 wi2)
  | wi2 => .det (.inc 0 wca)
  | wca => .det (.clr 2 wrow)
  | wrow => .det (.jeq 2 4 wcc wrc)
  | wrc => .det (.clr 3 (ak 1))
  | wrn => .det (.inc 2 wrow)
  | wcc => .det (.clr 3 (ak 2))
  | wrd => .det (.call 0 .whole [0] wcl rej)
  | wcl => .det (.clr 4 wcy)
  | wcy => .det (.jeq 4 8 wst wby)
  | wby => .det (.inc 4 wcy)
  | wst => .det (.inc 7 w0)
  | acc => .det (.ret true)
  | rej => .det (.ret false)

/-- **The machine meets the syntactic preconditions**: its comparisons are of distinct
registers and its calls have one argument. -/
lemma pathA_npreS (x : List Bool) (a : AConf 9 PathLabel) : NPreS pathA x a := by
  rcases a with ⟨_ | l, v, res⟩
  · trivial
  · cases l <;> simp [NPreS, PreS, NARM.detPart, pathA]
    all_goals (rename_i k; fin_cases k <;> simp [akY])

/-- The deciders of the walk machine: the input bit and input length languages. -/
def pathAs : Fin 2 → Language Bool := ![inputBitLang, inputLenLang]

/-- The deciders' answers. -/
noncomputable abbrev pathOr : Fin 2 → List Bool → Bool :=
  fun j V => MultiTapeTM.indicator (pathAs j : Set (List Bool)) V

/-- Decider `0` reads an input bit. -/
lemma pathOr_bit (x : List Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    pathOr 0 (pairEncode x (Nat.bits i)) = x.getD i false := by
  show MultiTapeTM.indicator (inputBitLang : Set (List Bool)) _ = _
  exact indicator_inputBitLang x i

/-- Decider `1` compares with the input length. -/
lemma pathOr_len (x : List Bool) (i : ℕ) :
    pathOr 1 (pairEncode x (Nat.bits i)) = decide (i < x.length) := by
  show MultiTapeTM.indicator (inputLenLang : Set (List Bool)) _ = _
  exact indicator_inputLenLang x i

/-- The deciders are in `L`. -/
lemma pathAs_mem (j : Fin 2) : pathAs j ∈ LOGSPACE := by
  fin_cases j
  · exact inputBitLang_mem
  · exact inputLenLang_mem

/-- The register file of the walk machine, by name. -/
@[ext] structure PReg where
  /-- the input pointer (register `0`) -/
  p : ℕ
  /-- the vertex count (register `1`) -/
  n : ℕ
  /-- the row counter (register `2`) -/
  a : ℕ
  /-- the column counter (register `3`) -/
  b : ℕ
  /-- the source, then the current vertex (register `4`) -/
  s : ℕ
  /-- the target (register `5`) -/
  t : ℕ
  /-- the scratch copy (register `6`) -/
  tmp : ℕ
  /-- the step count (register `7`) -/
  st : ℕ
  /-- the guessed next vertex (register `8`) -/
  nx : ℕ

/-- The register values of a register file. -/
def PReg.v (σ : PReg) : Fin 9 → ℕ := ![σ.p, σ.n, σ.a, σ.b, σ.s, σ.t, σ.tmp, σ.st, σ.nx]

/-- Every register of a register file is at most `B`. -/
def PReg.Le (σ : PReg) (B : ℕ) : Prop :=
  σ.p ≤ B ∧ σ.n ≤ B ∧ σ.a ≤ B ∧ σ.b ≤ B ∧ σ.s ≤ B ∧ σ.t ≤ B ∧ σ.tmp ≤ B ∧ σ.st ≤ B ∧ σ.nx ≤ B

/-- The register-bound guard from the named bounds. -/
lemma PReg.reg {σ : PReg} {B : ℕ} (h : σ.Le B) (l : Option PathLabel) (res : Option Bool) :
    RegLe 9 PathLabel B (l, σ.v, res) := by
  obtain ⟨h0, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, h7, h8⟩ := h
  intro r
  fin_cases r <;> assumption

section PRegSimp

variable (σ : PReg) (z : ℕ)

/-- Register `0` is the input pointer. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.v_0 : σ.v 0 = σ.p := rfl
/-- Register `1` is the vertex count. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.v_1 : σ.v 1 = σ.n := rfl
/-- Register `2` is the row counter. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.v_2 : σ.v 2 = σ.a := rfl
/-- Register `3` is the column counter. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.v_3 : σ.v 3 = σ.b := rfl
/-- Register `4` is the current vertex. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.v_4 : σ.v 4 = σ.s := rfl
/-- Register `5` is the target. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.v_5 : σ.v 5 = σ.t := rfl
/-- Register `6` is the scratch copy. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.v_6 : σ.v 6 = σ.tmp := rfl
/-- Register `7` is the step count. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.v_7 : σ.v 7 = σ.st := rfl
/-- Register `8` is the guessed vertex. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.v_8 : σ.v 8 = σ.nx := rfl

/-- Writing register `0` writes the input pointer. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.u_0 : Function.update σ.v 0 z = { σ with p := z }.v := by
  funext r; fin_cases r <;> rfl
/-- Writing register `1` writes the vertex count. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.u_1 : Function.update σ.v 1 z = { σ with n := z }.v := by
  funext r; fin_cases r <;> rfl
/-- Writing register `2` writes the row counter. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.u_2 : Function.update σ.v 2 z = { σ with a := z }.v := by
  funext r; fin_cases r <;> rfl
/-- Writing register `3` writes the column counter. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.u_3 : Function.update σ.v 3 z = { σ with b := z }.v := by
  funext r; fin_cases r <;> rfl
/-- Writing register `4` writes the current vertex. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.u_4 : Function.update σ.v 4 z = { σ with s := z }.v := by
  funext r; fin_cases r <;> rfl
/-- Writing register `5` writes the target. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.u_5 : Function.update σ.v 5 z = { σ with t := z }.v := by
  funext r; fin_cases r <;> rfl
/-- Writing register `6` writes the scratch copy. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.u_6 : Function.update σ.v 6 z = { σ with tmp := z }.v := by
  funext r; fin_cases r <;> rfl
/-- Writing register `7` writes the step count. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.u_7 : Function.update σ.v 7 z = { σ with st := z }.v := by
  funext r; fin_cases r <;> rfl
/-- Writing register `8` writes the guessed vertex. -/
@[simp] lemma PReg.u_8 : Function.update σ.v 8 z = { σ with nx := z }.v := by
  funext r; fin_cases r <;> rfl

end PRegSimp

open PathLabel

/-- The semantics of the walk machine at label `l` with register file `σ`, registers
bounded by `B`. -/
abbrev PS (x : List Bool) (B : ℕ) (l : PathLabel) (σ : PReg) (P : Prop) : Prop :=
  NSem pathA pathOr x (RegLe 9 PathLabel B) (some l, σ.v, none) P

variable {x : List Bool} {B : ℕ}

/-- Change the register file to an equal one. -/
lemma PS.of_eq {l : PathLabel} {σ σ' : PReg} {P : Prop} (h : σ = σ') (hp : PS x B l σ' P) :
    PS x B l σ P := h ▸ hp

namespace PathWalkTac

/-- Normalize reads and updates of a named register file of the walk machine. -/
scoped macro "pw_regs" : tactic => `(tactic| simp only [PReg.v_0, PReg.v_1, PReg.v_2, PReg.v_3,
  PReg.v_4, PReg.v_5, PReg.v_6, PReg.v_7, PReg.v_8, PReg.u_0, PReg.u_1, PReg.u_2, PReg.u_3,
  PReg.u_4, PReg.u_5, PReg.u_6, PReg.u_7, PReg.u_8])

/-- Prove a register bound of the walk machine by linear arithmetic. -/
scoped macro "pw_le" : tactic => `(tactic| (simp only [PReg.Le] at *; omega))

/-- Prove an equality of register files field by field. -/
scoped macro "pw_ext" : tactic => `(tactic| (ext <;> dsimp only <;> omega))

/-- Prove an equality of register files field by field, simplifying first. -/
scoped macro "pw_ext'" : tactic => `(tactic| (ext <;> (try simp) <;> (try omega)))

end PathWalkTac

open PathWalkTac

/-- **The row loop** of the index computation: from row `a ≤ s` with the pointer at the
start of row `a`, the machine reaches the start of row `s`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `s - a`: at `a = s` the loop exits; otherwise it clears the
column counter, adds `2n` to the pointer (`nsem_addTwice`) and increments the row. All
pointer values stay below the start of row `s`, inside the input. -/
lemma ps_row (hB : 2 * x.length + 2 ≤ B) (P : Prop) (σ : PReg) (hσ : σ.Le B)
    (hi : σ.a ≤ σ.s) (hs : σ.s < σ.n) (hp : σ.p = 2 * σ.n + 2 + 2 * (σ.a * σ.n))
    (hb : σ.b ≤ σ.n) (hm : 2 * σ.n + 2 + 2 * (σ.n * σ.n) ≤ x.length)
    (hK : ∀ b', b' ≤ σ.n →
      PS x B wcc { σ with a := σ.s, p := 2 * σ.n + 2 + 2 * (σ.s * σ.n), b := b' } P) :
    PS x B wrow σ P := by
  suffices H : ∀ d (σ : PReg), σ.s - σ.a = d → σ.Le B → σ.a ≤ σ.s → σ.s < σ.n →
      σ.p = 2 * σ.n + 2 + 2 * (σ.a * σ.n) → σ.b ≤ σ.n →
      2 * σ.n + 2 + 2 * (σ.n * σ.n) ≤ x.length →
      (∀ b', b' ≤ σ.n →
        PS x B wcc { σ with a := σ.s, p := 2 * σ.n + 2 + 2 * (σ.s * σ.n), b := b' } P) →
      PS x B wrow σ P from H _ σ rfl hσ hi hs hp hb hm hK
  intro d
  induction d with
  | zero =>
    intro σ hd hσ hi hs hp hb hm hK
    have he : σ.a = σ.s := by omega
    have he' : σ.a * σ.n = σ.s * σ.n := by rw [he]
    refine NSem.jeq_pos rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _) (by simpa using he) ?_
    exact PS.of_eq (by ext <;> simp <;> omega) (hK σ.b hb)
  | succ d ih =>
    intro σ hd hσ hi hs hp hb hm hK
    have hne : σ.a ≠ σ.s := by omega
    have h1 : (σ.a + 1) * σ.n ≤ σ.s * σ.n := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (by omega)
    have h2 : (σ.s + 1) * σ.n ≤ σ.n * σ.n := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (by omega)
    rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul] at h1 h2
    refine NSem.jeq_neg rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _) (by simpa using hne) ?_
    refine NSem.clr rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _) ?_
    pw_regs
    refine nsem_addTwice pathA pathOr x B 3 1 0 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
      (ak 1) (ak₁ 1) (ak₂ 1) (ak₃ 1) wrn rfl rfl rfl rfl _ _ (PReg.reg (by pw_le) none none)
      (by simp) (by simp; omega) ?_
    pw_regs
    refine NSem.inc rfl (PReg.reg (by pw_le) _ _) ?_
    pw_regs
    refine PS.of_eq (σ' := { σ with a := σ.a + 1, p := σ.p + 2 * σ.n, b := σ.n })
      (by ext <;> simp) ?_
    exact ih _ (by dsimp only; omega) (by pw_le) (by dsimp only; omega) hs
      (by dsimp only; rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul]; omega) le_rfl hm hK

/-- **The index computation**: the machine sets the pointer to the matrix position
`2n + 2 + 2(s · n + v)` of the edge from the current vertex `s` to the guessed vertex `v`.

**Proof sketch.** Clear the pointer, add `2n` (`nsem_addTwice`) and `2` to reach the
matrix, walk `s` rows (`ps_row`), then add `2v` (`nsem_addTwice`); the final position is
below `2n + 2 + 2n²`, inside the input (`rowMajor_lt`). -/
lemma ps_index (hB : 2 * x.length + 2 ≤ B) (P : Prop) (σ : PReg) (hσ : σ.Le B)
    (hs : σ.s < σ.n) (hj : σ.nx < σ.n) (hm : 2 * σ.n + 2 + 2 * (σ.n * σ.n) ≤ x.length)
    (hK : PS x B wrd
      { σ with p := 2 * σ.n + 2 + 2 * (σ.s * σ.n + σ.nx), a := σ.s, b := σ.nx } P) :
    PS x B wcp σ P := by
  have hidx := rowMajor_lt hs hj
  have h0 : σ.s * σ.n ≤ σ.n * σ.n := by omega
  refine NSem.clr rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _) ?_
  pw_regs
  refine NSem.clr rfl (PReg.reg (by pw_le) _ _) ?_
  pw_regs
  refine nsem_addTwice pathA pathOr x B 3 1 0 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
    (ak 0) (ak₁ 0) (ak₂ 0) (ak₃ 0) wi1 rfl rfl rfl rfl _ _ (PReg.reg (by pw_le) none none)
    (by simp) (by simp; omega) ?_
  pw_regs
  refine NSem.inc rfl (PReg.reg (by pw_le) _ _) ?_
  pw_regs
  refine NSem.inc rfl (PReg.reg (by pw_le) _ _) ?_
  pw_regs
  refine NSem.clr rfl (PReg.reg (by pw_le) _ _) ?_
  pw_regs
  refine ps_row hB P _ (by pw_le) (by simp) (by simpa using hs) (by dsimp only; omega) (by simp)
    (by simpa using hm) fun b' hb' => ?_
  simp only at hb' ⊢
  refine NSem.clr rfl (PReg.reg (by pw_le) _ _) ?_
  pw_regs
  refine nsem_addTwice pathA pathOr x B 3 8 0 (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
    (ak 2) (ak₁ 2) (ak₂ 2) (ak₃ 2) wrd rfl rfl rfl rfl _ _ (PReg.reg (by pw_le) none none)
    (by simp) (by simp; omega) ?_
  pw_regs
  exact PS.of_eq (by pw_ext') hK

/-- **The walk loop** [AB09, §4.1.2]: from the current vertex `s` after `st ≤ n` steps,
some branch accepts iff `t` is reachable from `s` within `n - st` edges; every branch
terminates.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `n - st`. At `s = t` the machine accepts; at `st = n` it
rejects; otherwise it guesses `v < n` (`nsem_guess`), computes the matrix position
(`ps_index`), rejects unless the edge bit is `1`, copies `v` into the current vertex
(`nsem_copy`) and counts the step. -/
theorem ps_walk (hB : 2 * x.length + 2 ≤ B) (σ : PReg) (hσ : σ.Le B) (hs : σ.s < σ.n)
    (ht : σ.t < σ.n) (hst : σ.st ≤ σ.n) (hm : 2 * σ.n + 2 + 2 * (σ.n * σ.n) ≤ x.length) :
    PS x B w0 σ (WalkLe (pathEdge x σ.n) σ.n (σ.n - σ.st) σ.s σ.t) := by
  suffices H : ∀ d (σ : PReg), σ.n - σ.st = d → σ.Le B → σ.s < σ.n → σ.t < σ.n →
      σ.st ≤ σ.n → 2 * σ.n + 2 + 2 * (σ.n * σ.n) ≤ x.length →
      PS x B w0 σ (WalkLe (pathEdge x σ.n) σ.n d σ.s σ.t) from H _ σ rfl hσ hs ht hst hm
  intro d
  induction d with
  | zero =>
    intro σ hd hσ hs ht hst hm
    by_cases he : σ.s = σ.t
    · refine (NSem.jeq_pos rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _) (by simpa using he)
        (NSem.ret rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _))).congr ?_
      simp only [WalkLe, he]
    · refine (NSem.jeq_neg rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _) (by simpa using he)
        (NSem.jeq_pos rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _) (by simp; omega)
          (NSem.ret rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _)))).congr ?_
      simp only [WalkLe, he, Bool.false_eq_true]
  | succ d ih =>
    intro σ hd hσ hs ht hst hm
    by_cases he : σ.s = σ.t
    · refine (NSem.jeq_pos rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _) (by simpa using he)
        (NSem.ret rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _))).congr ?_
      simp only [WalkLe, he, true_or]
    refine NSem.jeq_neg rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _) (by simpa using he) ?_
    refine NSem.jeq_neg rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _) (by simp; omega) ?_
    refine NSem.clr rfl (PReg.reg hσ _ _) ?_
    pw_regs
    refine (nsem_guess pathA pathOr x B 8 1 (by decide) wg wc wm wcp rej rfl rfl rfl rfl
      (fun j => pathEdge x σ.n σ.s j ∧ WalkLe (pathEdge x σ.n) σ.n d j σ.t) _
      (PReg.reg (by pw_le) none none) (by simp) (fun j hj1 hj2 => ?_)).congr ?_
    · simp only [PReg.v_8, PReg.v_1] at hj1 hj2
      pw_regs
      have hidx := rowMajor_lt hs hj2
      refine ps_index hB _ _ (by pw_le) (by simpa using hs) (by simpa using hj2)
        (by simpa using hm) ?_
      simp only
      by_cases hedge : pathEdge x σ.n σ.s j
      · refine NSem.call_pos rfl (PReg.reg (by pw_le) _ _)
          (by simp only [PReg.v_0, pathOr_bit]; exact hedge) ?_
        refine NSem.clr rfl (PReg.reg (by pw_le) _ _) ?_
        pw_regs
        refine nsem_copy pathA pathOr x B 4 8 (by decide) wcy wby wst rfl rfl _ _
          (PReg.reg (by pw_le) none none) (by simp) ?_
        pw_regs
        refine NSem.inc rfl (PReg.reg (by pw_le) _ _) ?_
        pw_regs
        let σ' : PReg :=
          ⟨2 * σ.n + 2 + 2 * (σ.s * σ.n + j), σ.n, σ.s, j, j, σ.t, σ.tmp, σ.st + 1, j⟩
        refine PS.of_eq (σ' := σ') (by simp only [σ']) ((ih σ' (by dsimp only [σ']; omega)
          (by simp only [σ', PReg.Le] at hσ ⊢; omega) (by dsimp only [σ']; omega) ht
          (by dsimp only [σ']; omega) hm).congr ?_)
        simp only [σ', hedge, true_and]
      · refine (NSem.call_neg rfl (PReg.reg (by pw_le) _ _)
          (by simp only [PReg.v_0, pathOr_bit]; simpa [pathEdge] using hedge)
          (NSem.ret rfl (PReg.reg (by pw_le) _ _))).congr ?_
        simp only [hedge, false_and, Bool.false_eq_true]
    · simp only [PReg.v_8, PReg.v_1, WalkLe, he, false_or]
      exact ⟨fun ⟨j, _, h⟩ => ⟨j, h.1, h.2⟩, fun ⟨j, h1, h2⟩ => ⟨j, Nat.zero_le _, h1, h2⟩⟩

end Complexity.LogProg
```

```
/-!
# Space complexity

Space-bounded computation and logarithmic space [AB09, §4.1, §4.3]: the classes `SPACE(s)`
and `L`, `L ⊆ P` by configuration counting, implicitly logspace computable functions and
their polynomial-time computability, with a toolkit of logspace machines (register-tape
programs calling logspace deciders on virtual inputs, and abstract register machines
compiled onto them).

Related model: `Complexity.CounterProg` (`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CounterProg`) is a
goto program over unary counters for the polynomial-time emitters of [AB09, §6.2]. It overlaps
in spirit with the programs here, which store registers in binary (as logarithmic space
requires) and call deciders on virtual inputs; the two are kept separate, and a polynomially
running counter program is simulated by an abstract register machine in
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.CounterProgSim`.

## Contents

- `SpaceComplexity.Basic`: Def 4.1 space-bounded computation, `SPACE(s)`, `L`; Def 4.16
  implicitly logspace computable functions
- `SpaceComplexity.ConfigCount`: configuration counting; `L ⊆ P`; logspace functions run in
  polynomial time
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.Layout`: virtual inputs assembled from segments
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.Program`: register-tape programs with call nodes and their
  compilation
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.Sim`: the lockstep simulation of a call's decider
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.CallReturn`: compiled configurations; the return phase of a call
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.Call`: the run of a call node
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.Compile`: correctness and space of compiled programs
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.CleanSweep`: the cleaned machine; the cleanup sweeps of one tape
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.Clean`: the clean normal form of deciders (the whole run)
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.Bank`: a bank of clean deciders
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.Bin`: binary words of numbers
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.Lib`: register steps and the increment fragment
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.FragDec`: decrement and clear fragments
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.Frag`: halve and equality fragments
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.ParsePlain`: input shapes; the format check on inputs `⟨1ⁿ, w⟩`
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.Parse`: comparisons on inputs `⟨1ⁿ, w⟩`
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.Parse2`: the format check on inputs `⟨1ⁿ, ⟨u, w⟩⟩`
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.ParseCmp`: comparisons on inputs `⟨1ⁿ, ⟨u, w⟩⟩`
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.ARM`: abstract register machines and their compilation
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.ARMSim`: per-instruction simulation
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.ARMRun`: the run and space theorems of compiled machines
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.ARMProof`: proving abstract machines correct; `arm_decides`
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.ARMKit`: calls on unary inputs; `arm_decides_poly`
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.ARMWidth`: abstract machines with wide registers;
  `arm_decides_space`, `arm_decides_SPACE`, `arm_decides_pspace`; `L ⊆ PSPACE`
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.ARMWidthExample`: exhaustive search over `|x|`-bit witnesses
  with a polynomially wide register (`PSPACE` is closed under it)
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.ARMReach`: compiled runs to live abstract configurations
  (`arm_step`, `arm_reach`)
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.NARM`: nondeterministic abstract register machines (`choose`),
  their choice-word semantics and correctness combinators
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.NARMCompile`: their compilation onto `FinNDTM`
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.NARMRun`: the run and space theorems of compiled
  nondeterministic machines (`narm_space`)
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.NARMProof`: `narm_decides_space`, `narm_decides` (`NL`),
  `narm_decides_npspace` (`NPSPACE`)
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.NARMExample`: a guessing machine deciding a language in `NL`
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.ARMLoops`: the bounded-run guard `GuardLe` and generic counting
  loops of abstract register machines
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.VWord`: small shared lemmas on reading inputs by index
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.NARMKit`: proving nondeterministic register machines correct by
  continuation (`NTerm`, `NAcc`, `NSem`), their step lemmas and generic nondeterministic
  loops
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.NARMProb`: compilation preserves acceptance probabilities when
  `choose` bits are fair coins (`narm_randProb`) [AB09, Def 7.1, §7.7]
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.NARMPSem`: the probabilistic continuation semantics `PSem` of
  such machines [AB09, §7.7]
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.NARMLogspace`: their compilation to logspace PTMs
  (`narm_logspace_ptm`) and the bridge `narm_mem_RL` to `RL` [AB09, §7.7]
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.DblLang`: reading the unary length `⟨1ⁿ, bits (2n)⟩` in
  logarithmic space
- `SpaceComplexity.ImplicitPoly`: implicitly logspace computable functions are
  polynomial-time computable
- `SpaceComplexity.UnaryLogspace`: functions of the unary length computable in logarithmic
  space (`UnaryLogspace`, `unaryExt`)
- `SpaceComplexity.CounterProgSim`, `SpaceComplexity.CounterProgSimRun`: polynomially
  running counter programs on unary-logspace inputs are unary-logspace
- `SpaceComplexity.NSPACE`: Def 4.1's nondeterministic clause, `NSPACE(s)` (chapters-3-4
  campaign, phase P4.1)
- `SpaceComplexity.SpaceClasses`: Def 4.5's `PSPACE`, `NPSPACE`, `NL`, and `coNL`
- `SpaceComplexity.Constructible`: space-constructible functions (p. 79)
- `SpaceComplexity.Inclusions`: Thm 4.2's first two inclusions; `P ⊆ PSPACE`;
  Example 4.6 (`NP ⊆ PSPACE`, `3SAT ∈ PSPACE`)
- `SpaceComplexity.Examples`: Example 4.7's parity language
- `SpaceComplexity.ZeroSpace`: the zero-bound collapse of unnormalized `SPACE` and the
  positive-normalization identities (P0 reception audit, round 1)
- `SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph`: configuration graphs and the ND Claim 4.4(1) (chapters-3-4
  campaign, phase P4.2; Thm 4.2(iii), `NL ⊆ P` and Ex 4.3 are in `SpaceComplexity.ExpTime`)
- `SpaceComplexity.WindowClock`: the windowed runner (host H3) under a configuration-count
  clock, window containment, and the windowed run of a halting space-bounded computation
  (the space hierarchy's window route; statement gate passed 2026-10-14)
- `SpaceComplexity.Savitch`: Savitch's theorem and `PSPACE = NPSPACE` (phase P4.2)
- `SpaceComplexity.Hierarchy`: the space-bounded universal machine, Thm 4.8,
  `L ⊊ PSPACE`, Ex 3.2 (phase P4.3)
- `SpaceComplexity.Logspace.{InputAccess, PreimageHost, QueryReshape}`: random access to a
  general input (a register-program read fragment; `id` implicitly logspace), the
  oracle-input simulator of Fig. 4.3 (logspace preimages along implicit functions), and the
  query reshapings of composition (phase P4.4b)
- `SpaceComplexity.Logspace.{Reductions, Path, ImmermanSzelepcsenyi, Mult}`: `≤ₗ` and
  Lemma 4.17, `PATH` and Thm 4.18, Thm 4.20 and Cor 4.21, `MULT ∈ L` (phase P4.4)
- `SpaceComplexity.Logspace.{PathWalk, PathWalkMachine, PathWalkProof}`: the
  nondeterministic walk deciding `PATH` (`PATH ∈ NL`, §4.1.2)
- `SpaceComplexity.Codec.{Word, Scan, Valid, Step, Langs, Checks}`: an `O(s + log n)`-bit
  codec for window-bounded configurations of a nondeterministic machine, the four code
  languages (valid, initial, accepting, step) and their word-level checks
- `SpaceComplexity.Codec.{Engine, Regs, Machine, Run, Parse, Layout, Layout2, Deciders,
  StepDecider}`: the four code languages are in `L` (an abstract register machine reading
  its input by index)
- `SpaceComplexity.Codec.Bridge`: acceptance of a space-bounded decider as a chain of codes
- `SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.{Reach, Machine, Run}`: midpoint reachability over codes; the
  Savitch register machine and its arithmetic and stack routines
- `SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.{Recursion, Setup, Search, Correct}`: the machine evaluates the
  midpoint recursion with an explicit stack; `NPSPACE ⊆ PSPACE` (Thm 4.14 at polynomial
  bounds, consumed by `PSPACE = NPSPACE` in `SpaceComplexity.Savitch`)
- `SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Window`: windows without a known space bound; no reachable
  edge code makes membership midpoint reachability at that radius, and none is reachable beyond
  the space bound (iterative deepening for Thm 4.14 without constructibility, after
  [Sip13, Thm 8.5])
- `SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Deepen`: the deepening machine, Savitch's search run as a block
  at radius `1, 2, …`; its contract gives Thm 4.14 for every `S ≥ logSpace`
- `SpaceComplexity.Machines.{MARM, MARMCompile, MARMTime}`: abstract register machines with
  a monotone memory tape, their compilation, and their time bound by configuration counting
  (`marm_dtime`)
- `SpaceComplexity.ExpBFS.{Radius, Machine, Run, Relax, Search, Main}`: reachable codes at
  growing radii; the breadth-first search memory machine;
  `NSPACE S ⊆ ⋃ c, DTIME (2 ^ (c (S n + 1)))` for `S ≥ logSpace`
- `SpaceComplexity.ExpTime`: Thm 4.2(iii), `NL ⊆ P`, Ex 4.3 (moved from
  `SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph`, after the codec)
- `SpaceComplexity.Logspace.{PathHard, PathHardRegs, PathHardMachine, PathHardWalk,
  PathHardRun, PathHardDecide}`: the configuration-graph reduction to `PATH`, the register
  file and deciders of its query register machine, the machine and its runs; every `NL`
  language logspace-reduces to `PATH` (Thm 4.18, consumed by `PATH_NLComplete` in
  `SpaceComplexity.Logspace.Path`)
- `SpaceComplexity.Logspace.{ISCountMath, ISCountRegs}`: the combinatorics of inductive
  counting (balls, guessed enumerations) and the register file of the counting machine
- `SpaceComplexity.Logspace.ISCountGen{Machine, Walk, Stage, Loop, Radius, Correct}`: the
  window-growing inductive-counting machine; `L ∈ NSPACE S → Lᶜ ∈ NSPACE S` for
  `S ≥ logSpace` (`compl_mem_NSPACE`, consumed by `NSPACE_compl_eq`, Cor 4.21) and its case
  `L ∈ NL → Lᶜ ∈ NL` (`compl_mem_NL`, consumed by `compl_PATH_mem_NL` and `NL_eq_coNL`,
  Thm 4.20)

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1, §4.3.)
-/
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/Constructible.lean =====

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Basic
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassP.TimeConstructible
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.InputLength
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.VirtualInput
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Seam
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Bin
import TCSlib.Complexity.ClassNP.Transducer
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.WordTests

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Space-constructible functions

[AB09, §4.1, p. 79]: `S : ℕ → ℕ` is space-constructible when some machine
computes `S(|x|)` from `x` within `O(S(|x|))` space, and the book's standing
convention is `S(n) > log n`. The definition mirrors
`Complexity.TimeConstructible` — output in binary (`Nat.bits`), constant slack
`c · S n`, which implements the book's own asymptotic space convention
([AB09, p. 79]: "computes `S(|x|)` in `O(S(|x|))` space"); an exact-space
variant is not posed here (the exact-**time** refutation of chapter 1 does not
transfer: a space deadline forces no premature halt) — and carries the book's
convention as the conjunct `∀ n, logSpace n ≤ S n`, so that downstream
statements (the space hierarchy, Savitch) can draw on it without restating it;
results needing only weaker hypotheses must say so.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.SpaceConstructible` — the binary-output, constant-slack,
  above-log form. [AB09, §4.1, p. 79]

## Main results (proved)

* `Complexity.spaceConstructible_iff` — the definition as an equivalence.
* `Complexity.spaceConstructible_logSpace` — `log` is space-constructible.
* `Complexity.spaceConstructible_linear` — `n + 1` is space-constructible.
* `Complexity.spaceConstructible_poly` — `n ^ c + 1` is space-constructible for `c ≥ 1`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1, p. 79.)
-/

namespace Complexity

open Turing

/-- A function `S` is **space-constructible** when it dominates the logarithm
(`Complexity.logSpace`, the book's standing `S(n) > log n` convention carried as
data) and some machine computes the binary representation of `S (|x|)` from `x`
within `c · S (|x|)` visited work-tape cells. Mirrors
`Complexity.TimeConstructible` (binary output via `Nat.bits`, constant slack).
[AB09, §4.1, p. 79] -/
def SpaceConstructible (S : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ n, logSpace n ≤ S n) ∧
  ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ M : FinTM Bool,
    M.ComputesInSpace (fun x => (S x.length).bits) fun n => c * S n

/-- **Space constructibility, unfolded**: `S` is space constructible exactly when
`logSpace n ≤ S n` for every `n` and, for some constant `c > 0`, some machine computes
`x ↦ (S |x|).bits` in space `c · S` (`Turing.FinTM.ComputesInSpace`). -/
theorem spaceConstructible_iff (S : ℕ → ℕ) :
    SpaceConstructible S ↔
      (∀ n, logSpace n ≤ S n) ∧ ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ M : FinTM Bool,
        M.ComputesInSpace (fun x => (S x.length).bits) fun n => c * S n :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- Positive binary words have exactly the normalized logarithmic width. -/
private lemma b3a_bits_length {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    n.bits.length = logSpace n := by
  have lower := Nat.lt_size.mpr (Nat.pow_log_le_self 2 hn)
  have upper := LogProg.length_bits_le_log n
  rw [← Nat.size_eq_bits_len] at lower
  unfold logSpace
  omega

/-- The counter word with its first cell overwritten by `true`. -/
private def b3a_word (n : ℕ) : List Bool := true :: n.bits.tail

/-- The overwrite handles zero while preserving every positive counter width. -/
private lemma b3a_word_length (n : ℕ) : (b3a_word n).length = logSpace n := by
  by_cases hn : n = 0
  · subst n
    simp [b3a_word, logSpace, Nat.bits]
  · simp only [b3a_word, List.length_cons, List.length_tail, b3a_bits_length hn]
    unfold logSpace
    omega

/-- Restricting a buffer to its occupied nonnegative interval does not change it. -/
private lemma b3a_buffer_restrict (w : List Bool) (z : ℤ) :
    (if 0 ≤ z ∧ z < (w.length : ℤ) then FinTM.bufferTape w z else none) =
      FinTM.bufferTape w z := by
  by_cases hzero : 0 ≤ z
  · by_cases hlast : z < (w.length : ℤ)
    · simp [hzero, hlast]
    · have out : w.length ≤ z.toNat := by omega
      simp [hzero, hlast, FinTM.bufferTape]
  · simp [hzero, FinTM.bufferTape]

/-- Setting the first buffered cell yields `true :: tail`, including an empty buffer. -/
private lemma b3a_buffer_overwrite (w : List Bool) (z : ℤ) :
    (if z = 0 then some true else FinTM.bufferTape w z) =
      FinTM.bufferTape (true :: w.tail) z := by
  by_cases hz : z = 0
  · subst z
    simp [FinTM.bufferTape]
  · by_cases hp : 0 ≤ z
    · have ht : z.toNat ≠ 0 := by omega
      simp only [if_neg hz, FinTM.bufferTape, if_pos hp, List.getElem?_cons,
        if_neg ht, List.getElem?_tail]
      congr 1
      omega
    · simp [hz, FinTM.bufferTape, hp]

/-- A live phase seam: its word is on tape zero and all heads are at the origin. -/
private def b3a_cfg {k : ℕ} [NeZero k] {S : Type} (s : S)
    (x w : List Bool) : Cfg k Bool S x :=
  { Cfg.init s x with
    workTapes := fun j => if j = 0 then FinTM.bufferTape w else fun _ => none }

/-- Map only the control field of a canonical phase seam. -/
private lemma b3a_cfg_map {k : ℕ} [NeZero k] {S T : Type} (f : S → T)
    (s : S) (x w : List Bool) :
    (b3a_cfg (k := k) s x w).mapState f = b3a_cfg (f s) x w := rfl

/-- Relocate a single-buffer seam along a selection preserving tape zero.
**Proof sketch.** Selected tapes use the public configuration projections;
other tapes use the frame theorem at time zero. All unused cells and heads are blank. -/
private lemma b3a_embed_cfg {m k : ℕ} [NeZero m] [NeZero k] {S : Type}
    (R : MultiTapeTM m Bool S) (ι : Fin m ↪ Fin k) (hzero : ι 0 = 0)
    (s : S) (x w : List Bool) :
    embedEmitCfg ι (fun _ _ => none) (fun _ => 0) [] (b3a_cfg s x w) =
      b3a_cfg (k := k) s x w := by
  apply Cfg.ext
  · rfl
  · rfl
  · funext j
    by_cases chosen : j ∈ Set.range ι
    · obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := chosen
      rw [embedEmitCfg_selected_tape]
      have hz : ι i = 0 ↔ i = 0 := by rw [← hzero, ι.injective.eq_iff]
      simp only [b3a_cfg, hz]
    · have frame := (embedEmitTM_frame ι R (fun _ _ => none) (fun _ => 0)
        [] (b3a_cfg s x w) 0).1 j chosen
      have hj : j ≠ 0 := fun eq => chosen ⟨0, hzero.trans eq.symm⟩
      simpa [b3a_cfg, hj] using frame.1
  · funext j
    by_cases chosen : j ∈ Set.range ι
    · obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := chosen
      rw [embedEmitCfg_selected_pos]
      rfl
    · exact (embedEmitTM_frame ι R (fun _ _ => none) (fun _ => 0)
        [] (b3a_cfg s x w) 0).1 j chosen |>.2
  · rfl

/-- A coarse constant-factor space bound for tape relocation.
**Proof sketch.** Every selected tape is bounded by the source's total space;
each unused tape contributes one cell. Sum this common bound over the host bank. -/
private lemma b3a_embed_space {m k : ℕ} {S : Type} {x : List Bool}
    (R : MultiTapeTM m Bool S) (ι : Fin m ↪ Fin k)
    (d : Cfg m Bool S x) (t : ℕ) :
    (embedEmitTM ι R).spaceUsed
        (embedEmitCfg ι (fun _ _ => none) (fun _ => 0) [] d) t ≤
      k * (R.spaceUsed d t + 1) := by
  unfold MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed
  calc
    _ ≤ ∑ _j : Fin k, (R.spaceUsed d t + 1) := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro j _
      by_cases chosen : j ∈ Set.range ι
      · obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := chosen
        rw [(embedEmitTM_visitedByTapeHead ι R (fun _ _ => none) (fun _ => 0) [] d t i).2]
        exact (R.spaceUsedByTape_le_spaceUsed d t i).trans (Nat.le_succ _)
      · rw [(embedEmitTM_visitedByTapeHead_frame ι R (fun _ _ => none)
          (fun _ => 0) [] d t j chosen).2]
        omega
    _ = _ := by simp [MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed]

/-- The additive space ledger for an arbitrary live-exit seam.
**Proof sketch.** Apply the public visited-set inclusion on each tape, bound
the cardinality of its union by the sum, and sum over the bank. -/
private lemma b3a_seam_space {k : ℕ} {S T : Type} [DecidableEq S] {x : List Bool}
    (R : MultiTapeTM k Bool S) (exit : S) (Q : MultiTapeTM k Bool T) (entry : T)
    {d e : Cfg k Bool S x} {a b : ℕ} (run : R.runFrom d a = e)
    (live : e.state = some exit) (cut : ∀ u < a, (R.runFrom d u).state ≠ some exit) :
    (seamCompTM R exit Q entry).spaceUsed (d.mapState Sum.inl) (a + 1 + b) ≤
      R.spaceUsed d a + Q.spaceUsed (e.mapState fun _ => entry) b := by
  calc
    _ ≤ ∑ i : Fin k, (R.spaceUsedByTape d a i +
        Q.spaceUsedByTape (e.mapState fun _ => entry) b i) := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro i _
      calc
        _ ≤ (R.visitedByTapeHead d a i ∪
            Q.visitedByTapeHead (e.mapState fun _ => entry) b i).card := by
          apply Finset.card_le_card
          exact seamCompTM_visitedByTapeHead_ofCfg R exit Q entry run live cut i
        _ ≤ _ := Finset.card_union_le _ _
    _ = _ := Finset.sum_add_distrib

/-- The public native counter, specialized to blank origin tapes with a cardinality ledger.
**Proof sketch.** Instantiate R8.5c at its entry, identify the globally blank frame
with the buffer layout, and enclose each head's visited set in the promised interval.
The first-exit clause is retained for the subsequent dispatch. -/
private theorem b3a_counter :
    ∃ (K : ℕ) (S : Type) (_ : Fintype S) (_ : DecidableEq S)
      (R : MultiTapeTM (K + 1) Bool S) (entry exit : S) (B : ℕ),
      ∀ x : List Bool, ∃ t,
        R.runFrom (b3a_cfg entry x []) t = b3a_cfg exit x x.length.bits ∧
        (∀ u < t, (R.runFrom (b3a_cfg entry x []) u).state ≠ some exit) ∧
        R.spaceUsed (b3a_cfg entry x []) t ≤ B * (x.length.bits.length + 1) := by
  obtain ⟨K, S, fs, ds, R, entry, exit, C, contract⟩ := exists_inputLengthTM
  letI := fs
  letI := ds
  refine ⟨K, S, fs, ds, R, entry, exit, (K + 1) * (2 * C + 1), ?_⟩
  intro x
  obtain ⟨t, _, cut, heads, finished⟩ := contract (b3a_cfg entry x []) rfl rfl
    (by intros; simp [b3a_cfg]) (by intros; simp [b3a_cfg])
  refine ⟨t, ?_, cut, ?_⟩
  · rw [finished]
    apply Cfg.ext
    · rfl
    · rfl
    · funext j z
      by_cases hj : j = 0
      · simp [b3a_cfg, hj, b3a_buffer_restrict]
      · simp [b3a_cfg, hj]
    · rfl
    · rfl
  · have perTape (j : Fin (K + 1)) : R.spaceUsedByTape (b3a_cfg entry x []) t j ≤
        2 * (C * (x.length.bits.length + 1)) + 1 := by
      calc
        _ ≤ (Finset.Icc (-((C * (x.length.bits.length + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ))
            ((C * (x.length.bits.length + 1) : ℕ) : ℤ)).card := by
          apply Finset.card_le_card
          intro z hz
          obtain ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hz
          have bound := heads u (Nat.le_of_lt_succ (Finset.mem_range.mp hu)) j
          simpa [b3a_cfg, Finset.mem_Icc, abs_le] using bound
        _ = _ := by rw [Int.card_Icc]; omega
    calc
      _ ≤ ∑ _j : Fin (K + 1), (2 * (C * (x.length.bits.length + 1)) + 1) :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum fun j _ => perTape j
      _ = (K + 1) * (2 * (C * (x.length.bits.length + 1)) + 1) := by simp
      _ ≤ (K + 1) * ((2 * C + 1) * (x.length.bits.length + 1)) := by
        apply Nat.mul_le_mul_left
        ring_nf; omega
      _ = _ := by ring

/-- The public constant writer overwrites cell zero and returns to its origin.
**Proof sketch.** Use R8.4 with `[true]`. Its four-step trace supplies the exact
exit cut and two-cell head interval; the buffer update is the tail identity above. -/
private theorem b3a_overwrite (x w : List Bool) :
    (writeConstTM 1 0 [true]).runFrom (b3a_cfg (.wr 0) x w) 4 =
        b3a_cfg .done x (true :: w.tail) ∧
      (∀ u < 4, ((writeConstTM 1 0 [true]).runFrom
        (b3a_cfg (.wr 0) x w) u).state ≠ some .done) ∧
      (writeConstTM 1 0 [true]).spaceUsed (b3a_cfg (.wr 0) x w) 4 ≤ 2 := by
  obtain ⟨run, cut, heads⟩ := writeConstTM_run_ofCfg (0 : Fin 1) [true]
    (b3a_cfg (.wr 0) x w) rfl
  norm_num only [List.length_singleton] at run
  refine ⟨?_, cut, ?_⟩
  · rw [run]
    apply Cfg.ext
    · rfl
    · rfl
    · funext j z
      have hj : j = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
      simp only [b3a_cfg, Cfg.init, hj, if_pos, List.length_singleton,
        zero_add, sub_zero]
      simp only [true_and, show (0 ≤ z ∧ z < 1) ↔ z = 0 by omega]
      by_cases hz : z = 0
      · simp [hz, FinTM.bufferTape]
      · simpa [hz] using b3a_buffer_overwrite w z
    · rfl
    · rfl
  · change ∑ j : Fin 1, _ ≤ 2
    rw [Fintype.sum_subsingleton _ (0 : Fin 1)]
    calc
      _ ≤ (Finset.Icc (0 : ℤ) 1).card := by
        apply Finset.card_le_card
        intro z hz
        obtain ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hz
        simpa [b3a_cfg] using heads 0 u (Nat.le_of_lt_succ (Finset.mem_range.mp hu))
      _ = 2 := by decide

/-- The emitting phase shares tape zero and places its bank after the native counter bank. -/
private def b3a_virtualSelect (K m : ℕ) : Fin (1 + m) ↪ Fin (K + 1 + m) where
  toFun i := ⟨if i.val = 0 then 0 else K + i.val, by split_ifs <;> omega⟩
  inj' := by
    intro i j eq
    apply Fin.ext
    have vals := congrArg Fin.val eq
    dsimp at vals
    split_ifs at vals <;> omega

/-- The initial virtual-input layout is the single-buffer phase seam.
**Proof sketch.** Split the host tapes into its buffer and source bank. The source
starts at input position one, with blank work tapes and all heads at zero. -/
private lemma b3a_virtual_cfg (L : FinTM Bool) (x y : List Bool) :
    vhostCfg (L.tm.initCfg y) true (1 : Fin (x.length + 2)) [] =
      b3a_cfg (L.tm.q₀, true) x y := by
  apply Cfg.ext
  · rfl
  · rfl
  · funext j z
    refine Fin.addCases (fun i => ?_) (fun i => ?_) j
    · have hi : i = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
      subst i
      have zero : Fin.castAdd L.k (0 : Fin 1) = 0 := rfl
      change FinTM.bufferTape y z =
        (if Fin.castAdd L.k (0 : Fin 1) = 0 then FinTM.bufferTape y else fun _ => none) z
      rw [if_pos zero]
    · have nonzero : Fin.natAdd 1 i ≠ (0 : Fin (1 + L.k)) := by
        intro eq
        have vals := congrArg Fin.val eq
        simp only [Fin.coe_natAdd, Fin.val_zero] at vals
        omega
      simp only [vhostCfg, Fin.addCases_right, b3a_cfg, if_neg nonzero,
        MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init]
  · funext j
    refine Fin.addCases (fun i => ?_) (fun i => ?_) j
    · simp [vhostCfg, b3a_cfg, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init]
    · simp [vhostCfg, b3a_cfg, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init]
  · rfl

/-- Assemble the three public phases with an explicit boundary-inclusive space allowance.
**Proof sketch.** Count on a native bank, overwrite its first cell, then host the
length counter on that word. Both seams dispatch at their first exits. The public
relocation and seam ledgers bound total space by a fixed multiple of the normalized
logarithm plus one; the final virtual-input halt emits the full binary answer. -/
private theorem b3a_log_machine :
    ∃ (A : ℕ), 0 < A ∧ ∃ M : FinTM Bool,
      M.ComputesInSpace (fun x => (logSpace x.length).bits)
        (fun n => A * (logSpace n + 1)) := by
  obtain ⟨K, S, fs, ds, R, entry, exit, B, counter⟩ := b3a_counter
  letI := fs
  letI := ds
  obtain ⟨L, b, computes, space⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_lengthBits_spaceUsed
  let k := K + 1 + L.k
  let ic : Fin (K + 1) ↪ Fin k := Fin.castAddEmb L.k
  let iw : Fin 1 ↪ Fin k := Fin.castLEEmb (by dsimp [k]; omega)
  let iv := b3a_virtualSelect K L.k
  have ic0 : ic 0 = 0 := rfl
  have iw0 : iw 0 = 0 := rfl
  have iv0 : iv 0 = 0 := by apply Fin.ext; simp [iv, b3a_virtualSelect]
  let C := embedEmitTM ic R
  let W := embedEmitTM iw (writeConstTM 1 0 [true])
  let E := embedEmitTM iv (vhostEmitTM L.tm)
  let CW := seamCompTM C exit W (.wr 0)
  let H := seamCompTM CW (Sum.inr .done) E (L.tm.q₀, true)
  let M : FinTM Bool :=
    { k := k
      State := (S ⊕ WritePhase 1) ⊕ (L.State × Bool)
      tm := {H with q₀ := Sum.inl (Sum.inl entry)} }
  refine ⟨k * (B + b + 8) + 1, by omega, M, ?_⟩
  intro x
  let y := b3a_word x.length
  obtain ⟨t, counted, countCut, countSpace⟩ := counter x
  obtain ⟨written, writeCut, writeSpace⟩ := b3a_overwrite x x.length.bits
  -- Count and overwrite share the buffer; their first-exit cuts justify both dispatches.
  have countRun : C.runFrom (b3a_cfg entry x []) t =
      b3a_cfg exit x x.length.bits := by
    rw [← b3a_embed_cfg R ic ic0 entry x [], embedEmitTM_runFrom, counted,
      b3a_embed_cfg R ic ic0]
  have countFirst : ∀ u < t, (C.runFrom (b3a_cfg entry x []) u).state ≠ some exit := by
    intro u hu
    rw [← b3a_embed_cfg R ic ic0 entry x [], embedEmitTM_runFrom]
    exact countCut u hu
  have writeRun : W.runFrom (b3a_cfg (.wr 0) x x.length.bits) 4 =
      b3a_cfg .done x y := by
    rw [← b3a_embed_cfg (writeConstTM 1 0 [true]) iw iw0 (.wr 0) x x.length.bits,
      embedEmitTM_runFrom, written, b3a_embed_cfg (writeConstTM 1 0 [true]) iw iw0]
    rfl
  have writeFirst : ∀ u < 4,
      (W.runFrom (b3a_cfg (.wr 0) x x.length.bits) u).state ≠ some .done := by
    intro u hu
    rw [← b3a_embed_cfg (writeConstTM 1 0 [true]) iw iw0 (.wr 0) x x.length.bits,
      embedEmitTM_runFrom]
    exact writeCut u hu
  have cwRun : CW.runFrom (b3a_cfg (Sum.inl entry) x []) (t + 1 + 4) =
      b3a_cfg (Sum.inr .done) x y := by
    simpa only [b3a_cfg_map] using seamCompTM_run_ofCfg C exit W (.wr 0)
      countRun rfl countFirst (by simpa only [b3a_cfg_map] using writeRun)
  have cwFirst : ∀ u < t + 1 + 4,
      (CW.runFrom (b3a_cfg (Sum.inl entry) x []) u).state ≠ some (Sum.inr .done) := by
    simpa only [b3a_cfg_map] using seamCompTM_firstReturn_ofCfg C exit W (.wr 0) .done
      countRun rfl countFirst (by simpa only [b3a_cfg_map] using writeRun) rfl
      (by simpa only [b3a_cfg_map] using writeFirst)
  -- The last phase forwards the hosted counter's full output, including its halting step.
  let u := b * (y.length + 1)
  have tag : FinTM.VirtualTag (L.tm.initCfg y).inputPos true := by
    simp [FinTM.VirtualTag, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Cfg.init]
  obtain ⟨tagEnd, _, hosted⟩ := vhostEmitTM_runFrom L.tm (L.tm.initCfg y) true tag
    (1 : Fin (x.length + 2)) [] u
  have emitted : E.runFrom (b3a_cfg (L.tm.q₀, true) x y) u =
      embedEmitCfg iv (fun _ _ => none) (fun _ => 0) []
        (vhostCfg (L.tm.runFrom (L.tm.initCfg y) u) tagEnd (1 : Fin (x.length + 2)) []) := by
    rw [← b3a_embed_cfg (vhostEmitTM L.tm) iv iv0 (L.tm.q₀, true) x y,
      ← b3a_virtual_cfg, embedEmitTM_runFrom, hosted]
  have fullRun := seamCompTM_run_ofCfg CW (Sum.inr .done) E (L.tm.q₀, true)
    cwRun rfl cwFirst (by simpa only [b3a_cfg_map] using emitted)
  have start : M.tm.initCfg x = b3a_cfg (Sum.inl (Sum.inl entry)) x [] := by
    apply Cfg.ext <;> simp [M, MultiTapeTM.initCfg, b3a_cfg, Cfg.init]
  refine ⟨(t + 1 + 4) + 1 + u, ?_, ?_⟩
  · apply (FinTM.computesInTime_iff _ _ _ _).mpr
    rw [start]
    change (H.runFrom _ _).state = none ∧ (H.runFrom _ _).output = _
    rw [show b3a_cfg (Sum.inl (Sum.inl entry)) x [] =
      (b3a_cfg (Sum.inl entry) x []).mapState Sum.inl from rfl, fullRun]
    obtain ⟨halted, output⟩ := (FinTM.computesInTime_iff L y _ u).mp (computes y)
    simp only [Cfg.mapState, embedEmitCfg, vhostCfg, List.nil_append,
      halted, output, Option.map_none, y, b3a_word_length, and_self]
  · rw [start]
    change H.spaceUsed _ _ ≤ _
    -- Add the three boundary-inclusive ledgers before absorbing the constant slack.
    have firstLedger := b3a_seam_space C exit W (.wr 0) (b := 4)
      countRun rfl countFirst
    have lastLedger := b3a_seam_space CW (Sum.inr .done) E (L.tm.q₀, true) (b := u)
      cwRun rfl cwFirst
    simp only [b3a_cfg_map] at firstLedger lastLedger
    have cSpace := b3a_embed_space R ic (b3a_cfg entry x []) t
    rw [b3a_embed_cfg R ic ic0] at cSpace
    have wSpace := b3a_embed_space (writeConstTM 1 0 [true]) iw
      (b3a_cfg (.wr 0) x x.length.bits) 4
    rw [b3a_embed_cfg (writeConstTM 1 0 [true]) iw iw0] at wSpace
    have eSpace := b3a_embed_space (vhostEmitTM L.tm) iv
      (vhostCfg (L.tm.initCfg y) true (1 : Fin (x.length + 2)) []) u
    rw [b3a_virtual_cfg, b3a_embed_cfg (vhostEmitTM L.tm) iv iv0] at eSpace
    have eSource := vhostEmitTM_spaceUsed_le L.tm (L.tm.initCfg y) true tag
      (1 : Fin (x.length + 2)) [] u
    rw [b3a_virtual_cfg] at eSource
    have sizeBound : Nat.size y.length ≤ y.length := by
      rw [← Nat.size_eq_bits_len]
      exact length_bits_le_self _
    have width := LogProg.length_bits_le_log x.length
    have yLength : y.length = logSpace x.length := b3a_word_length _
    have nativeBound : C.spaceUsed (b3a_cfg entry x []) t ≤
        k * (B * (logSpace x.length + 1) + 1) := by
      apply cSpace.trans
      apply Nat.mul_le_mul_left
      apply Nat.add_le_add_right
      exact countSpace.trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left B (Nat.add_le_add_right width 1))
    have writerBound : W.spaceUsed (b3a_cfg (.wr 0) x x.length.bits) 4 ≤ k * 3 := by
      exact wSpace.trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega))
    have emitterBound : E.spaceUsed (b3a_cfg (L.tm.q₀, true) x y) u ≤
        k * (b * (logSpace x.length + 1) + logSpace x.length + 3) := by
      apply eSpace.trans
      apply Nat.mul_le_mul_left
      have ls := space y u
      have bound := (Nat.mul_le_mul_left b (Nat.add_le_add_right sizeBound 1))
      rw [yLength] at bound eSource ls
      omega
    calc
      _ ≤ C.spaceUsed (b3a_cfg entry x []) t +
          W.spaceUsed (b3a_cfg (.wr 0) x x.length.bits) 4 +
          E.spaceUsed (b3a_cfg (L.tm.q₀, true) x y) u :=
        lastLedger.trans (Nat.add_le_add_right firstLedger _)
      _ ≤ k * (B * (logSpace x.length + 1) + 1) + k * 3 +
          k * (b * (logSpace x.length + 1) + logSpace x.length + 3) := by
        exact Nat.add_le_add (Nat.add_le_add nativeBound writerBound) emitterBound
      _ ≤ (k * (B + b + 8) + 1) * (logSpace x.length + 1) := by
        ring_nf; omega

/-- **The logarithm is space-constructible.** [AB09, p. 79: "all functions of
interest, including `log n`, …, are space-constructible"]

**Proof sketch.** Fill obligations: a machine that (i) counts the input length
in binary on a work tape by one left-to-right input scan with a binary
increment at each step (the `Turing.counterTM`/`incrementTM` idiom — P11 of
`machine-library-design.md` §4, space-annotated per §12 R3) — the counter word
has `|Nat.bits n| = logSpace n` cells **for `n > 0` only** (`Nat.bits 0 = []`
has length `0 ≠ logSpace 0 = 1`), so (ii) the empty
input is special-cased to emit `(logSpace 0).bits = [true]` directly, and
otherwise the machine computes the counter word's bit-length by a second count
and emits its bits. Space: the counters and markers fit in
`A·(logSpace n + 1) ≤ 2A·logSpace n` visited cells (boundary cells included
before absorbing, since `logSpace n ≥ 1`); the dominance conjunct is `le_refl`
at `S = logSpace`.

**Fill appendix.** The empty-input special case is realized uniformly: after
R8.5c counts the native input, the constant writer sets the first buffered cell
to `true`. The resulting word has length `logSpace n`, including at zero. A
Z1-hosted Catalog length counter emits its binary length and genuinely halts.
Both live exits are intercepted at their first visits. The space ledger includes
the native head intervals, the overwrite boundary, the virtual-input boundary
cells and the fresh bank, giving `A * (logSpace n + 1)` before absorption. -/
theorem spaceConstructible_logSpace : SpaceConstructible logSpace := by
  obtain ⟨A, hA, M, hM⟩ := b3a_log_machine
  refine ⟨fun _ => le_rfl, 2 * A, by omega, M, ?_⟩
  intro x
  obtain ⟨t, ht, hs⟩ := hM x
  refine ⟨t, ht, hs.trans ?_⟩
  have hlog : logSpace x.length + 1 ≤ 2 * logSpace x.length := by
    unfold logSpace
    omega
  calc
    A * (logSpace x.length + 1) ≤ A * (2 * logSpace x.length) :=
      Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ hlog
    _ = (2 * A) * logSpace x.length := by ring

/-- **Linear space is constructible**: `n ↦ n + 1` is space-constructible (the
`+ 1` prevents the inherited zero-bound collapse at `n = 0` — the zero-bound
convention, `SpaceComplexity/ZeroSpace.lean` — and satisfies the dominance
conjunct; zero-space classes are nonempty, so this is about collapse, not
vacuity).

**Proof sketch.** The input-scan counter of
`Complexity.spaceConstructible_logSpace`, **initialized at `1`** so that after
`n` consumed symbols it holds `n + 1` (an uncorrected length counter holds `n`
and emits the wrong word); emit its bits. Space:
the counter's binary width plus fixed administrative cells fit in
`A·(n + 2) ≤ 2A·(n + 1)` visited cells; dominance is `logSpace n ≤ n + 1`
(`1 ≤ 1` at `n = 0`; a small arithmetic lemma otherwise).

**Fill appendix.** The counter initialized at `1` is realized by the Catalog
length counter on `true :: x`, using the proved prepend and buffered-composition
rows. Its linear running time bounds all visited work-tape cells, including
the counter width and boundary cells. -/
theorem spaceConstructible_linear : SpaceConstructible fun n => n + 1 := by
  refine ⟨logSpace_le_succ, ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨P, a, hp, _⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_prepend_spaceUsed [true]
  obtain ⟨L, b, hl, _⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_lengthBits_spaceUsed
  let M := FinTM.bufferedCompTM P L
  refine ⟨M.k * (a + 2 * b + 4) + 1, by omega, M, ?_⟩
  intro x
  let t := a * (x.length + 1) + (x.length + 1) + 2 + b * (x.length + 2)
  refine ⟨t, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simpa [M, t] using FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computesInTime P L (hp x) (hl ([true] ++ x))
  · have ht : t + 1 ≤ (a + 2 * b + 4) * (x.length + 1) := by
      dsimp [t]
      ring_nf; omega
    calc
      M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) t ≤ M.k * (t + 1) :=
        M.tm.spaceUsed_le_mul_succ _ _
      _ ≤ M.k * ((a + 2 * b + 4) * (x.length + 1)) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ ht
      _ ≤ (M.k * (a + 2 * b + 4) + 1) * (x.length + 1) := by
        rw [← Nat.mul_assoc]
        exact Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.le_succ _)

/-- The tail transducer's transition: one bit of state, "the first bit has been read". -/
private def scp_tailδ : Bool → Bool → Bool := fun _ _ => true

/-- The tail transducer's emission: nothing on the first bit, the bit itself afterwards. -/
private def scp_tailO : Bool → Bool → Option Bool := fun q b => if q then some b else none

/-- After the first bit the tail transducer copies its input. -/
private theorem scp_transduce_copy (l : List Bool) : transduce scp_tailδ scp_tailO true l = l :=
  transduce_of_copy _ _ true (fun _ => rfl) (fun _ => rfl) l

/-- From its start state the tail transducer computes `List.tail`. -/
private theorem scp_transduce_tail (x : List Bool) :
    transduce scp_tailδ scp_tailO false x = x.tail := by
  cases x with
  | nil => exact transduce_nil _ _ _
  | cons b l =>
    rw [transduce_cons]
    simp only [scp_tailO, scp_tailδ, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, Option.toList_none,
      List.nil_append, scp_transduce_copy, List.tail_cons]

/-- The unary intermediate is short: `(|x.tail| + 1) ^ c ≤ |x| ^ c + 1`. -/
private theorem scp_tail_pow_le (c : ℕ) (x : List Bool) :
    (x.tail.length + 1) ^ c ≤ x.length ^ c + 1 := by
  cases x with
  | nil => simp
  | cons b l => simp

/-- The conditional's value: for `1 ≤ c`, the branch function is `x ↦ (|x| ^ c + 1).bits`
(`0 ^ c + 1 = 1` on the empty input; otherwise the count of `true :: 1ᴾ` with
`P = (|x.tail| + 1) ^ c = |x| ^ c`). -/
private theorem scp_value (c : ℕ) (hc : 1 ≤ c) (x : List Bool) :
    (if decide (x = []) then Nat.bits 1
      else Nat.bits (true :: List.replicate (1 * (x.tail.length + 1) ^ c) true).length) =
      Nat.bits (x.length ^ c + 1) := by
  cases x with
  | nil =>
    simp only [decide_true, if_true, List.length_nil]
    rw [zero_pow (by omega), Nat.zero_add]
  | cons b l =>
    simp only [reduceCtorEq, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false, List.length_cons,
      List.length_replicate, Nat.one_mul, List.tail_cons]

/-- The main branch's time, as arithmetic: with `P = (|x.tail| + 1) ^ c ≤ N + 1`, `N = |x| ^ c`,
and `|x.tail| ≤ |x|`, the four phases' exact times sum to at most
`(5c + 20 + 3c_L)(N + |x| + 1)`. -/
private theorem scp_time_arith (c cL t n P N : ℕ) (hP : P ≤ N + 1) (ht : t ≤ n) :
    n + 1 + t + 2 + (1 + 5 * c + 4) * P + P + 2 + (0 + 1 + P + 1) + (0 + 1 + P) + 2 +
      cL * (0 + 1 + P + 1) ≤ (5 * c + 20 + 3 * cL) * (N + n + 1) := by
  have h1 := Nat.mul_le_mul_left (1 + 5 * c + 4) hP
  have h2 := Nat.mul_le_mul_left cL hP
  nlinarith [h1, h2, Nat.zero_le (c * n), Nat.zero_le (cL * n), Nat.zero_le (cL * N),
    Nat.zero_le (c * N)]

/-- The conditional's time, as arithmetic: with `n ≤ N`, the bound
`c_M (c_D (n + 1) + max (c₁ (n + 1)) (K (N + n + 1)) + 1) + 1` is at most `A (N + 1)` for
`A = c_M (c_D + c₁ + 2K + 2) + 1`. -/
private theorem scp_space_arith (cM cD c₁ K n N : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ N) :
    cM * (cD * (n + 1) + max (c₁ * (n + 1)) (K * (N + n + 1)) + 1) + 1 ≤
      (cM * (cD + c₁ + 2 * K + 2) + 1) * (N + 1) := by
  have hmax : max (c₁ * (n + 1)) (K * (N + n + 1)) ≤ c₁ * (n + 1) + K * (N + n + 1) :=
    max_le_add_of_nonneg (Nat.zero_le _) (Nat.zero_le _)
  have e1 := Nat.mul_le_mul_left cD hn
  have e2 := Nat.mul_le_mul_left c₁ hn
  have e3 := Nat.mul_le_mul_left K hn
  have hin : cD * (n + 1) + max (c₁ * (n + 1)) (K * (N + n + 1)) + 1 ≤
      (cD + c₁ + 2 * K + 2) * (N + 1) := by
    nlinarith [hmax, e1, e2, e3]
  have h4 := Nat.mul_le_mul_left cM hin
  nlinarith [h4, Nat.zero_le (cM * (cD + c₁ + 2 * K + 2))]

/-- **Polynomial bounds are space-constructible** [AB09, p. 79]: for `1 ≤ c`, the normal-form
bound `n ^ c + 1` is `Complexity.SpaceConstructible`. (Degree zero is excluded: `n ^ 0 + 1 = 2`
fails the bundled `logSpace n ≤ S n` at large `n`; consumers route degree
zero through monotonicity into degree one.)

**Proof sketch.** Dominance: `logSpace n ≤ n + 1 ≤ n ^ c + 1` (`Complexity.logSpace_le_succ`,
and `n ≤ n ^ c` for `1 ≤ c`). The witness machine computes
`x ↦ (|x| ^ c + 1).bits` as a timed conditional on `x = []`
(`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_cond`, with the decider
`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_decideEq []`). On the empty input the constant
writer emits `(1).bits`, which is the value since `0 ^ c + 1 = 1`. Otherwise four phases run by
buffered composition (`Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computesInTime`), each at its exact time:
1. a two-state transducer drops the first bit (`Complexity.transducerTM_computes`; from its
   second state it copies, `Complexity.transduce_of_copy`);
2. the unary generator `polyUnaryTM 1 c` writes `(|x| - 1 + 1) ^ c = |x| ^ c` ones;
3. `prependTM [true]` adds one more;
4. the length counter emits the binary length `|x| ^ c + 1`.
The four times sum to `O(|x| ^ c + |x| + 1)`, because the unary word has length at most
`|x| ^ c + 1`, so the conditional halts within `A (|x| ^ c + 1)` steps for a constant `A`
(`|x| ≤ |x| ^ c`). Space follows from time: a `k`-tape machine visits at most `k (t + 1)`
work-tape cells in `t` steps (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_le_mul_succ`), which gives the
space constant `k A + 1`. -/
theorem spaceConstructible_poly (c : ℕ) (hc : 1 ≤ c) :
    SpaceConstructible fun n => n ^ c + 1 := by
  -- the published rows
  obtain ⟨L, cL, hL⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_lengthBits
  obtain ⟨D, cD, hD'⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_decideEq []
  obtain ⟨K₁, c₁, hK₁⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_const (Nat.bits 1)
  let T := transducerTM scp_tailδ scp_tailO false
  let U := FinTM.polyUnaryTM 1 c
  let P := FinTM.prependTM [true]
  let N := FinTM.bufferedCompTM (FinTM.bufferedCompTM (FinTM.bufferedCompTM T U) P) L
  let f₂ : List Bool → List Bool := fun x =>
    Nat.bits (true :: List.replicate (1 * (x.tail.length + 1) ^ c) true).length
  -- the main branch, input by input: exact times of the four phases, composed
  have hN : N.ComputesFunInTime f₂ fun n => (5 * c + 20 + 3 * cL) * (n ^ c + n + 1) := by
    apply (FinTM.computesFunInTime_iff _ _ _).mpr
    intro x
    have hT : T.ComputesInTime x x.tail (x.length + 1) := by
      have h := (FinTM.computesFunInTime_iff _ _ _).mp
        (transducerTM_computes scp_tailδ scp_tailO false) x
      rwa [scp_transduce_tail] at h
    have hU := (FinTM.computesFunInTime_iff _ _ _).mp (FinTM.polyUnaryTM_computes 1 c) x.tail
    have hP := (FinTM.computesFunInTime_iff _ _ _).mp (FinTM.prependTM_computes [true])
      (List.replicate (1 * (x.tail.length + 1) ^ c) true)
    have hL' := (FinTM.computesFunInTime_iff _ _ _).mp hL
      ([true] ++ List.replicate (1 * (x.tail.length + 1) ^ c) true)
    have h₁ := FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computesInTime T U hT hU
    have h₂ := FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computesInTime _ P h₁ hP
    have h₃ := FinTM.bufferedCompTM_computesInTime _ L h₂ hL'
    apply h₃.mono
    have hp := scp_tail_pow_le c x
    have htl : x.tail.length ≤ x.length := by simp
    simp only [List.length_replicate, Nat.one_mul, List.length_append, List.length_cons,
      List.length_nil]
    exact scp_time_arith c cL x.tail.length x.length _ _ hp htl
  obtain ⟨M, cM, hM⟩ := FinTM.computesFunInTime_cond hD' hK₁ hN
  -- the value
  have hval : (fun x : List Bool => if decide (x = []) then Nat.bits 1 else f₂ x) =
      fun x => Nat.bits (x.length ^ c + 1) := by
    funext x
    exact scp_value c hc x
  rw [hval] at hM
  -- time, then space from time
  refine (spaceConstructible_iff _).mpr ⟨fun n => ?_,
    M.k * (cM * (cD + c₁ + 2 * (5 * c + 20 + 3 * cL) + 2) + 1) + 1, by omega, M, ?_⟩
  · have h1 := logSpace_le_succ n
    have h2 : n ≤ n ^ c := Nat.le_self_pow (by omega) n
    omega
  · apply (FinTM.computesInSpace_iff _ _ _).mpr
    intro x
    refine ⟨_, (FinTM.computesFunInTime_iff _ _ _).mp hM x, ?_⟩
    apply (MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_le_mul_succ _ _ _).trans
    have hB := scp_space_arith cM cD c₁ (5 * c + 20 + 3 * cL) x.length (x.length ^ c)
      (Nat.le_self_pow (by omega) x.length)
    calc M.k * (cM * (cD * (x.length + 1) + max (c₁ * (x.length + 1))
            ((5 * c + 20 + 3 * cL) * (x.length ^ c + x.length + 1)) + 1) + 1)
        ≤ M.k * ((cM * (cD + c₁ + 2 * (5 * c + 20 + 3 * cL) + 2) + 1) * (x.length ^ c + 1)) :=
          Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ hB
      _ ≤ (M.k * (cM * (cD + c₁ + 2 * (5 * c + 20 + 3 * cL) + 2) + 1) + 1) *
            (x.length ^ c + 1) := by
        rw [← Nat.mul_assoc]
        exact Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.le_succ _)

end Complexity
```
